result.unit_or_currency: sets of Template Attribute Values, no unit
result.stored_or_displayed: used to reopen a configurator on a workable configuration; never stored

edge_cases.case: The desired combination is already possible.
edge_cases.outcome: It is the first element emitted and nothing is given up.

edge_cases.case: The desired combination is empty and nothing is possible.
edge_cases.outcome: The stream is empty and the explanatory text says that no combination is possible.

edge_cases.case: Every member has to be dropped.
edge_cases.outcome: The last iteration runs with no necessary values, so the answer is the template's own first possible combination.

edge_cases.case: The desired combination is incomplete but consistent.
edge_cases.outcome: The remaining lines are enumerated and the missing answers are filled from the first possible values.

worked_examples.description: A pre-filled link asking for an excluded pair
worked_examples.narrative: With both values necessary there are no remaining lines and the predicate refuses the pair, so the stream is empty. The members are ordered by line sequence, ten before twenty, so the colour is dropped. The second iteration enumerates the colour line, rejects the excluded pair and keeps the other: the buyer keeps the size asked for and loses the colour.

records.name: The extra price carried by a variant's own members
records.purpose: Sums the supplements declared by the values stored on a variant, which is the part of the variant's price that distinguishes it from its template.

operands.name: extra price of each Template Attribute Value in the variant's combination
operands.source: the Template Attribute Values stored on the variant
operands.constraints: may be zero, positive or negative; all summands are in the template's currency

preconditions.condition: Every summand is expressed in the template's currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The sum would mix currencies; by construction the extra prices are held in that one currency, so no conversion takes place inside the sum.

procedure: Take the Template Attribute Values stored on the variant.
Sum their extra prices in the template's currency.
Apply no rounding to the sum itself; it is a decimal shown at the `Product Price` precision.
records.formula: variant_price_extra = sum_of( price_extra of each Template Attribute Value in the variant combination )

rounding.what: The displayed sum.
rounding.precision: The `Product Price` decimal precision, two digits by default.
rounding.step: At display only; the stored sum is not rounded and no summand is rounded before being added.

result.name: variant price extra
result.stored_or_displayed: computed on the Product Variant and displayed beside its sales price; also passed to the price computation as part of the attributes extra price

edge_cases.case: The variant has no member.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is zero, which is the case of a template with no attribute line.

edge_cases.case: A member carries a negative extra price.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum may be negative and the variant may be cheaper than its template; no floor is applied.

edge_cases.case: A member belongs to an attribute that never creates variants but is still stored after a mode change.
edge_cases.outcome: It is summed here, and the context-borne extra deliberately excludes members already in the variant's combination so that it is not counted twice.

edge_cases.case: A named unit of measure is in the context.
edge_cases.outcome: The extra is not converted; only the template's price is, which is the asymmetry the variant's sales price rule states.

worked_examples.description: A variant carrying two supplements
worked_examples.narrative: Five plus two is seven in the template's currency, displayed with two decimals because the `Product Price` precision is two digits.

worked_examples.description: A variant carrying a rebate on one member
worked_examples.narrative: Nothing floors the sum at zero, so a value declared with a negative supplement makes the variant cheaper than its template.

records.name: The sales price of a variant in the product's own unit of measure
records.purpose: Gives the price a variant shows when no unit of measure is named in the reading context: the template's price plus the variant's own supplements.

operands.name: template sales price
operands.unit_or_currency: the template's currency, per the product's default unit of measure
operands.source: the Product Template
operands.constraints: read as zero when unset

operands.name: variant price extra
operands.source: the sum of the extra prices of the variant's members
operands.constraints: may be zero, positive or negative

preconditions.condition: No unit of measure is named in the reading context.
preconditions.otherwise: The template price is converted into the named unit first and the extra is added afterwards, unconverted.

procedure: Read the template's sales price in the template's currency.
Add the variant's price extra.
Display the result at the `Product Price` precision.
records.formula: variant_sales_price_in_product_unit = template_sales_price + variant_price_extra

rounding.what: The displayed sales price.
rounding.precision: The `Product Price` decimal precision, two digits by default.
rounding.step: At display; the addition is performed on unrounded figures.

result.name: variant sales price
result.unit_or_currency: the template's currency, per the product's default unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: computed and displayed on the Product Variant; writing it inverts the computation onto the template's sales price

edge_cases.case: The template's sales price is unset.
edge_cases.outcome: It is read as zero and the variant's price is its extra alone.

edge_cases.case: The extra is negative and larger in size than the template price.
edge_cases.outcome: The variant's sales price is negative; nothing clamps it.

edge_cases.case: The variant has no member.
edge_cases.outcome: The variant's sales price equals the template's.

worked_examples.description: The dearest variant of the office chair
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred plus seven, both in the template's currency and both per unit of the product's own unit of measure.

records.name: The sales price of a variant read in a named unit of measure
records.purpose: States how a variant's price is expressed when the reading context names another unit of measure: the template's price is converted and the attribute supplement is added afterwards, unconverted.

operands.name: template sales price
operands.unit_or_currency: the template's currency, per the product's default unit of measure
operands.source: the Product Template
operands.constraints: read as zero when unset

operands.name: absolute factor of the named unit of measure
operands.source: the unit named in the reading context
operands.constraints: the factor convention is the one of the units of measure and packaging domain

operands.name: absolute factor of the product's default unit of measure
operands.source: the product's own unit of measure
operands.constraints: must be non-zero

operands.name: variant price extra
operands.source: the sum of the extra prices of the variant's members
operands.constraints: never converted between units at this step

preconditions.condition: A unit of measure is named in the reading context and both units belong to the same category.
preconditions.otherwise: No conversion takes place and the price is the one in the product's own unit.

procedure: Convert the template's sales price by multiplying it by the named unit's absolute factor and dividing by the product unit's absolute factor.
Add the variant's price extra to the converted figure, without converting the extra.
Display the result at the `Product Price` precision.
records.formula: variant_sales_price_in_named_unit = ( template_sales_price × named_unit_absolute_factor ÷ product_unit_absolute_factor ) + variant_price_extra

rounding.what: The displayed converted price.
rounding.precision: The `Product Price` decimal precision, two digits by default.
rounding.step: After the conversion and after the addition, at display; the division is not rounded before the extra is added.

result.name: variant sales price in the named unit of measure
result.unit_or_currency: the template's currency, per the named unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed to the caller that named the unit; not stored

edge_cases.case: The named unit equals the product's own unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The two factors cancel and the price is the template's price plus the extra.

edge_cases.case: The extra is non-zero and the named unit is larger than the product's own.
edge_cases.outcome: The supplement is under-stated relative to the converted template price, because it is deliberately not converted; this asymmetry is real and must be reproduced.

edge_cases.case: The product's unit factor is missing.
edge_cases.outcome: No conversion is attempted and the price in the product's own unit is used.

worked_examples.description: Reading a variant's price in dozens
worked_examples.narrative: One dozen contains twelve units, so the template price of one hundred per unit becomes one thousand two hundred per dozen. The seven of attribute supplement is added as it stands, not multiplied by twelve, giving one thousand two hundred and seven.

records.name: The template sales price derived from a variant price that is written
records.purpose: Inverts the variant price computation so that typing a price on a variant stores the corresponding price on its template, the attribute supplement being taken back out.

operands.name: written price
operands.unit_or_currency: the template's currency, per the unit named in the context or per the product's own unit
operands.source: the user or the caller writing the variant's sales price
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: absolute factor of the product's default unit of measure and of the named unit
operands.source: the two units of measure
operands.constraints: applied only when a unit is named in the context

operands.name: variant price extra
operands.source: the sum of the extra prices of the variant's members
operands.constraints: subtracted after the conversion, never converted itself

preconditions.condition: The variant belongs to the template whose price is about to be rewritten.
preconditions.otherwise: Writing the price of one variant would change the price of another template's products.

procedure: Convert the written price back into the product's own unit by multiplying by the product unit's absolute factor and dividing by the named unit's absolute factor, and skip that step when no unit was named.
Subtract the variant's price extra from the converted figure.
Store the result as the template's sales price, at the `Product Price` precision.
Note the consequence: writing the price of one variant moves the price of every variant of the template, because only the template's price is stored.
records.formula: new_template_sales_price = ( written_price × product_unit_absolute_factor ÷ named_unit_absolute_factor ) − variant_price_extra

rounding.what: The stored template sales price.
rounding.precision: The `Product Price` decimal precision, two digits by default.
rounding.step: At storage, after the division and after the subtraction, so that intermediate digits are not lost before the supplement is removed.

result.name: template sales price
result.unit_or_currency: the template's currency, per the product's default unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the Product Template

edge_cases.case: The division does not terminate.
edge_cases.outcome: The quotient is carried unrounded into the subtraction and the result is stored at the `Product Price` precision, so the stored figure may not reproduce the written one exactly when read back.

edge_cases.case: No unit is named in the context.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the supplement is subtracted.

edge_cases.case: The supplement exceeds the converted price.
edge_cases.outcome: A negative template price is stored; the negativity check of the domain applies to the cost, not to the sales price.

worked_examples.description: Writing a price in dozens on a variant carrying a supplement
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand three hundred per dozen is one hundred and eight point three three three three per unit; taking out the seven of supplement leaves one hundred and one point three three three three, stored at the two digits of the `Product Price` precision as one hundred and one point three three.

records.name: The extra price of chosen values that never create a variant, on a variant
records.purpose: Carries the supplements of the values a buyer chose that are not stored on any variant, so that a configured option is charged without multiplying the catalogue.

operands.name: chosen combination
operands.unit_or_currency: a set of Template Attribute Values, no unit
operands.source: the configurator or the document line
operands.constraints: complete, holding both the variant's own members and the members that never reach a variant

operands.name: extra price of each chosen member
operands.source: each Template Attribute Value
operands.constraints: only members with a non-zero extra price take part

operands.name: the variant's own combination members
operands.unit_or_currency: a set of Template Attribute Values, no unit
operands.source: the variant
operands.constraints: used to exclude members that are already counted in the variant's own extra

preconditions.condition: The chosen member belongs to the variant's template.
preconditions.otherwise: It is not summed, so a value of another template cannot add to this product's price.

preconditions.condition: The test excludes members already in the variant's own combination rather than looking at the attribute's mode.
preconditions.otherwise: An attribute whose mode was changed after the variants were built would have its supplement counted twice.

procedure: Take the members of the chosen combination whose extra price is not zero.
Keep those that belong to this variant's template.
Drop those that are among the variant's own combination members.
Sum the extra prices of what remains.
Pass the sum as the context entry `no_variant_attributes_price_extra` (extra price of attributes that create no variant) to the price computation.
records.formula: no_variant_attributes_price_extra = sum_of( price_extra of each Template Attribute Value V in the chosen combination such that V.price_extra ≠ 0 and V belongs to this variant's template and V is not one of this variant's own combination members )

rounding.what: The displayed sum.
rounding.precision: The `Product Price` decimal precision, two digits by default.
rounding.step: At display and when the sum reaches a document line; the summands are added unrounded.

result.name: extra price of the values that never create a variant
result.stored_or_displayed: passed through the price context and added to the unit price of the document line; not stored on the variant

edge_cases.case: A chosen member has a zero extra price.
edge_cases.outcome: It is skipped by the first condition, which costs nothing and keeps the sum short.

edge_cases.case: A chosen member is already stored on the variant.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded here, because the variant's own extra already carries it.

edge_cases.case: The chosen combination names a value of another template.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded, so a parent product's supplement never leaks into this line.

edge_cases.case: No value of an attribute that never creates variants was chosen.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is zero and the unit price is the variant's own price.

worked_examples.description: A pack with a paper attribute that creates variants and an engraving attribute that never does
worked_examples.narrative: The glossy paper is already on the variant, so only the gold foil qualifies, at twelve. Adding the variant's own four gives sixteen of supplement, and twenty-five plus sixteen is forty-one. Because the chosen value is flagged as free text, an Attribute Custom Value record holds the typed text and its computed name joins the value's name and the text.

records.name: The attributes extra price of a variant
records.purpose: Adds the two sources of supplement a configured variant carries, which is the amount the price computation adds to the sales price before any unit conversion.

operands.name: variant price extra
operands.source: the sum of the extra prices of the variant's stored members
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: extra price of the chosen values that never create a variant
operands.source: the price context entry carrying the chosen combination's remaining supplements
operands.constraints: zero when the context carries no such entry

preconditions.condition: The two sums are disjoint, the second excluding every member already in the variant's combination.
preconditions.otherwise: A supplement would be charged twice on the same line.

procedure: Take the variant's own price extra.
Add the extra price carried by the chosen values that never create a variant.
Hand the total to the price computation, which adds it to the sales price before any unit conversion.
records.formula: variant_attributes_extra_price = variant_price_extra + no_variant_attributes_price_extra

rounding.what: The displayed total supplement.
rounding.precision: The `Product Price` decimal precision, two digits by default.
rounding.step: At display; the addition itself is exact and unrounded.

result.name: attributes extra price of the variant
result.stored_or_displayed: added to the sales price inside the price computation; not stored

edge_cases.case: The context carries no chosen combination.
edge_cases.outcome: The second term is zero and the total is the variant's own extra.

edge_cases.case: The price kind being computed is the cost.
edge_cases.outcome: The supplement is not added at all: only the sales price takes the attributes extra price.

edge_cases.case: A unit of measure is named in the price computation.
edge_cases.outcome: The supplement is added before the conversion and is therefore converted, which is the opposite of the variant's own sales-price field.

worked_examples.description: The configured pack of business cards
worked_examples.narrative: Four of paper supplement stored on the variant plus twelve of engraving supplement carried by the context gives sixteen.

records.name: The attributes extra price of a template
records.purpose: Gives the supplement to add while a configuration is still being chosen and no variant exists yet, for instance in a configurator or on a dynamic template.

operands.name: chosen combination
operands.unit_or_currency: a set of Template Attribute Values, no unit
operands.source: the configurator
operands.constraints: may be partial

operands.name: extra price of each chosen member
operands.source: each Template Attribute Value
operands.constraints: only members with a non-zero extra price take part

preconditions.condition: The chosen members belong to this template.
preconditions.otherwise: They are not summed.

preconditions.condition: No variant is being priced.
preconditions.otherwise: The variant form applies instead, which subtracts the members already stored on the variant.

procedure: Take the members of the chosen combination whose extra price is not zero and that belong to this template.
Sum their extra prices; no member is excluded, because no variant holds any of them yet.
Pass the sum as the context entry `current_attributes_price_extra` (extra price of the attributes currently chosen) to the price computation, where it is the template's attributes extra price.
records.formula:
current_attributes_price_extra = sum_of( price_extra of each Template Attribute Value V in the chosen combination such that V.price_extra ≠ 0 and V belongs to this template )
template_attributes_extra_price = current_attributes_price_extra

rounding.what: The displayed sum.
rounding.precision: The `Product Price` decimal precision, two digits by default.
rounding.step: At display; the summands are added unrounded.

result.name: attributes extra price of the template
result.stored_or_displayed: added to the template's sales price inside the price computation; not stored

edge_cases.case: The configurator has answered only some of the questions.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the answered members are summed, so the price shown grows as the buyer answers.

edge_cases.case: The same combination is later priced through a variant.
edge_cases.outcome: The variant form splits the same total between the variant's own extra and the context-borne extra, and the two totals agree.

edge_cases.case: No member has a non-zero extra.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is zero and the template's own sales price is shown.

worked_examples.description: Pricing a configuration before any variant exists
worked_examples.narrative: With no variant to own the paper supplement, both members are summed on the template side, giving the same forty-one the variant form produces once the variant exists.

records.name: The price computation of a template or a variant for the sales price
records.purpose: Produces the sales price of each record in a target unit of measure and a target currency, which is the figure a pricelist, a document line or a storefront starts from.

operands.name: raw sales price of the record
operands.unit_or_currency: the record's currency, per the product's default unit of measure
operands.source: the sales price field of the template or of the variant, read as zero when unset
operands.constraints: the price kind is the stored value `list_price` (sales price)

operands.name: attributes extra price
operands.source: the variant form or the template form of the attributes extra price, taken from the price context
operands.constraints: added only for the sales price, never for the cost

operands.name: target unit of measure and the product's own unit
operands.source: the caller and the product
operands.constraints: the conversion is skipped when the units are the same, when the amount is zero or when either unit is missing

operands.name: target currency, company and date
operands.unit_or_currency: a currency, a company and a date
operands.source: the caller; the company defaults to the acting company and the date to today in the reader's time zone
operands.constraints: the conversion delegates to the multi-currency domain

preconditions.condition: The records are re-read in the context of the company that was chosen.
preconditions.otherwise: A company-dependent price would be read for the wrong company.

preconditions.condition: The source currency of the sales price is the record's own currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The conversion would start from the wrong currency.

procedure: Default the company to the acting company and the date to today in the reader's time zone.
Re-read the records in the context of that company.
Take the raw sales price of each record, or zero when it is unset.
Take the record's currency as the source currency.
Add the attributes extra price.

Convert to the target unit when one was given, by multiplying by the target unit's absolute factor and dividing by the product unit's absolute factor, and skip the conversion when the two units are the same, when the amount is zero or when either unit is missing.
Convert from the source currency to the target currency when one was given, for the chosen company and date.
Note the evaluation order: the supplement is added before the unit conversion, so here the supplement is converted, which is the opposite of the variant's own sales-price field.
records.formula:
amount = raw_sales_price + attributes_extra_price
converted = amount × target_unit_absolute_factor ÷ source_unit_absolute_factor
sales_price = convert_currency( converted, from = record_currency, to = target_currency, company, date )

rounding.what: The converted amount.
rounding.precision: The `Product Price` decimal precision for display, two digits by default; the currency conversion rounds to the target currency's rounding multiple.
rounding.step: After the unit conversion and after the currency conversion; the addition of the supplement happens first and is not rounded.

result.name: sales price in the target unit and currency
result.unit_or_currency: the target currency, per the target unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: returned to the caller, one amount per record; not stored

edge_cases.case: The amount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit conversion is skipped, so zero stays zero whatever the units.

edge_cases.case: The target unit equals the product's own unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion is skipped and the amount passes through unchanged.

edge_cases.case: No target currency is given.
edge_cases.outcome: The amount stays in the record's own currency.

edge_cases.case: The record is a template and the caller supplied a chosen combination.
edge_cases.outcome: The template form of the attributes extra price is added, so a configurator sees the same total the variant will later show.

worked_examples.description: Pricing a configured variant in dozens through the price computation
worked_examples.narrative: The supplement is added first, giving one hundred and seven per unit, and the whole of that is multiplied by twelve, giving one thousand two hundred and eighty-four per dozen. The variant's own sales-price field would instead have produced one thousand two hundred and seven, because it converts first and adds afterwards; both behaviours exist and both must be reproduced.

worked_examples.description: Pricing with a currency conversion and no unit change

inputs.target_currency: a currency worth 1.25 units per euro

worked_examples.narrative: No unit is named, so only the currency conversion applies: fifty multiplied by one point two five is sixty-two point five zero, rounded to the target currency's rounding multiple.

records.name: The price computation of a template or a variant for the cost
records.purpose: Produces the cost of each record in a target unit of measure and a target currency, reading it as a privileged reader and falling back to the first variant's cost on a template whose own cost is zero.

operands.name: raw cost of the record
operands.unit_or_currency: the record's cost currency, per the product's default unit of measure
operands.source: the cost field of the template or of the variant, read as zero when unset
operands.constraints: the price kind is the stored value `standard_price` (cost)

operands.name: cost of the template's first variant
operands.source: the first variant of the template
operands.constraints: used only on a template, only for the cost, and only when the template's own cost came back as zero and the template has variants

operands.name: target unit of measure and the product's own unit
operands.source: the caller and the product
operands.constraints: the conversion is skipped when the units are the same, when the amount is zero or when either unit is missing

operands.name: target currency, company and date
operands.unit_or_currency: a currency, a company and a date
operands.source: the caller; the company defaults to the acting company and the date to today in the reader's time zone
operands.constraints: the conversion delegates to the multi-currency domain

preconditions.condition: The records are re-read in the context of the chosen company and as a privileged reader.
preconditions.otherwise: The cost is readable only by internal users, and a sales price that has to be derived from it could not be produced for anybody else.

procedure: Default the company to the acting company and the date to today in the reader's time zone.
Re-read the records in the context of that company and additionally as a privileged reader, because the cost is readable only by internal users.
Take the raw cost of each record, or zero when it is unset.
Take the record's cost currency as the source currency.
On a template only, when the template's own cost came back as zero and the template has variants, take the first variant's cost instead.
Add no attributes extra price: the supplement belongs to the sales price alone.
Convert to the target unit when one was given, and skip the conversion when the two units are the same, when the amount is zero or when either unit is missing.
Convert from the cost currency to the target currency when one was given, for the chosen company and date.
records.formula:
amount = raw_cost
amount = first_variant_cost   when the record is a template, raw_cost = 0 and the template has variants
converted = amount × target_unit_absolute_factor ÷ source_unit_absolute_factor
cost = convert_currency( converted, from = record_cost_currency, to = target_currency, company, date )

rounding.what: The converted amount.
rounding.precision: The `Product Price` decimal precision for display, two digits by default; the currency conversion rounds to the target currency's rounding multiple.
rounding.step: After the unit conversion and after the currency conversion; the fallback to the first variant's cost happens before either.

result.name: cost in the target unit and currency
result.unit_or_currency: the target currency, per the target unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: returned to the caller, one amount per record; not stored by this computation

edge_cases.case: The template's own cost is zero and it has no variant.
edge_cases.outcome: No fallback is possible and zero is returned.

edge_cases.case: The template's own cost is zero and its first variant's cost is also zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Zero is returned and the unit conversion is skipped, because the amount is zero.

edge_cases.case: The reader is an external user.
edge_cases.outcome: The privileged read still yields the cost, so a sales price derived from the cost can be produced.

edge_cases.case: The cost is negative because it was written through an import or a remote call.
edge_cases.outcome: It is converted and returned as it stands; the refusal of a negative cost is an interface warning, not a stored constraint.

worked_examples.description: Reading the cost of a template whose own cost is unset
worked_examples.narrative: The template's own cost comes back as zero and the template has variants, so the first variant's cost of eighteen point four zero is used instead. No unit or currency conversion applies.

worked_examples.description: Reading a variant's cost in a larger unit
worked_examples.narrative: Two point five zero per unit multiplied by twelve is thirty per dozen; no attributes extra price is added, because the supplement belongs to the sales price alone.

records.name: The base price of a choice group
records.purpose: Gives each choice group of a combination product the weight by which the combination's price is shared out: the cheapest of the products the group offers.

operands.name: sales price of each item's variant, supplements included
operands.source: each combo item of the choice group, taking the variant's sales price with its own attribute supplements
operands.constraints: the group must hold at least one item for the minimum to exist

operands.name: currency of each item's variant
operands.source: the item's variant
operands.constraints: each item is converted separately before the minimum is taken

operands.name: currency of the choice group
operands.source: the choice group
operands.constraints: the target of the conversion

operands.name: company and moment of the conversion
operands.unit_or_currency: a company and a moment in time
operands.source: the choice group's company or, failing that, the acting company; the current moment
operands.constraints: the conversion is made at the current moment, not at the order date

preconditions.condition: The choice group holds at least one item.
preconditions.otherwise: The base price is zero, and a choice group with no item is refused by the business rules in any case.

procedure: For each item of the group, take its variant's sales price including that variant's own attribute supplements.
Convert each of those prices from the item variant's currency into the choice group's currency, for the group's company or the acting company, at the current moment.
Take the smallest of the converted prices.
Report zero when the group holds no item.
records.formula:
choice_base_price = minimum over items of convert( item_variant_sales_price, from = item_variant_currency, to = choice_currency, company = choice_company or acting_company, date = current_moment )
choice_base_price = 0 when the group has no item

rounding.what: Each converted item price before the minimum is taken.
rounding.precision: The choice group currency's rounding multiple for the conversion, and the `Product Price` decimal precision for display, two digits by default.
rounding.step: At the conversion of each item, before the minimum; the minimum itself rounds nothing.

result.name: base price of the choice group
result.stored_or_displayed: computed live and displayed on the choice group; deliberately not stored, because the conversion uses the current moment

edge_cases.case: The group holds no item.
edge_cases.outcome: The base price is zero; the proration then falls into its equal-share branch when every group is in that state.

edge_cases.case: The currency rate changes between two reads.
edge_cases.outcome: The base price changes, because the conversion is made at the current moment rather than at a stored date; two reads of the same record may differ.

edge_cases.case: Two items have the same lowest price.
edge_cases.outcome: The minimum is that price; which item carries it does not matter, because only the amount is used.

edge_cases.case: An item's variant carries a negative attribute supplement.
edge_cases.outcome: Its sales price may be the lowest and may even be negative; the minimum is taken as it stands.

worked_examples.description: The three choice groups of a lunch menu, all in the document currency
worked_examples.narrative: Each conversion is an identity because every price is already in euro, so each group's base price is simply the cheapest item it offers: eight, three point five zero and two.

records.name: The price of a combination product before it is prorated
records.purpose: Establishes the single amount that the child lines of a combination product must add up to: the price the combination product would have had if it were an ordinary product.

operands.name: pricelist price of the combination product
operands.source: the pricelist applied to the document line, with combination logic deliberately ignored
operands.constraints: computed as for any ordinary product

operands.name: pre-discount base price
operands.source: the applicable pricelist rule, when that rule displays a discount
operands.constraints: used only when the rule displays a discount

preconditions.condition: The document line carries a combination product.
preconditions.otherwise: No proration takes place and the line prices itself as an ordinary product.

procedure: Compute the price the combination product would have had as an ordinary product, ignoring combination logic entirely.
When the applicable pricelist rule displays a discount, take the larger of the pre-discount base price and the pricelist price instead.
Use that amount as the total to be shared out over the choice groups.
records.formula:
combo_product_price = pricelist_price                                            when the rule displays no discount
combo_product_price = maximum( pre_discount_base_price , pricelist_price )       when the rule displays a discount

rounding.what: The price taken from the pricelist.
rounding.step: As the pricelist produces the price, before any proration.

result.name: combination product price
result.stored_or_displayed: used as the total of the proration; the combination product's own line displays zero, so the amount appears only through the child lines

edge_cases.case: No pricelist rule applies.
edge_cases.outcome: The catalogue price of the combination product is used.

edge_cases.case: The rule displays a discount and the pre-discount base price is the lower of the two.
edge_cases.outcome: The pricelist price wins, because the larger of the two is taken.

edge_cases.case: The price is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Every share is zero and the child lines carry only their own item supplements.

worked_examples.description: A menu with no applicable pricelist rule
worked_examples.narrative: With no rule to apply, the price to share out is the catalogue price of fifteen.

worked_examples.description: A rule that displays a discount
worked_examples.narrative: Because the rule displays a discount, the larger of the two amounts is prorated, so the child lines add up to fifteen and the discount is shown separately.

records.name: The converted base prices and the total base price of a combination product
records.purpose: Brings every choice group's base price into the document's currency at the document's date and adds them, giving the denominator of the proration.

operands.name: base price of each choice group
operands.source: the base price of each choice group of the combination product
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: document currency, document company and document date
operands.unit_or_currency: a currency, a company and a date
operands.source: the document carrying the combination product
operands.constraints: the conversion is made at the document date, not at the current moment

preconditions.condition: The document has a currency, a company and a date.
preconditions.otherwise: No conversion can be made and the proration cannot run.

procedure: For each choice group of the combination product, convert its base price from the group's currency into the document currency, for the document company, at the document date.
Add the converted base prices to obtain the total base price.
Keep the individual converted base prices, because each is the numerator of its group's share.
records.formula:
converted_base_price( g ) = convert( base_price( g ), choice_currency( g ), document_currency, document_company, document_date )
total_base_price = sum over g of converted_base_price( g )

rounding.what: Each converted base price.
rounding.step: At each conversion, before the sum; the sum itself rounds nothing further.

result.name: converted base price per choice group and total base price
result.stored_or_displayed: used inside the proration; not stored

edge_cases.case: Every group's base price is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The total is zero and the proration switches to its equal-share branch.

edge_cases.case: The document currency equals every group's currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversions are identities and the total is the plain sum of the base prices.

edge_cases.case: The document date is in the past.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate of that date is used, so the proration is stable when the document is re-read, unlike the base price itself.

worked_examples.description: Three groups already in the document currency
worked_examples.narrative: Eight plus three point five zero plus two is thirteen point five zero, the denominator every share is divided by.

records.name: The prorated share of a choice group when the total base price is not zero
records.purpose: Splits the combination product's price between its choice groups in proportion to their base prices, which is what makes each child line carry a plausible share of the revenue.

operands.name: converted base price of the choice group
operands.source: the base price of the group converted at the document date
operands.constraints: may be zero for an individual group as long as the total is not

operands.name: combination product price
operands.source: the price the combination product would have had as an ordinary product
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: total base price
operands.source: the sum of the converted base prices of every choice group
operands.constraints: must not be zero for this branch to apply

preconditions.condition: The total base price is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The equal-share branch applies instead, because prorating by zero weights would concentrate the whole price on one group through the remainder correction.

procedure: Multiply the group's converted base price by the combination product price.
Divide by the total base price.
Round the quotient to the document currency's rounding multiple, half away from zero.
Repeat for every choice group, then apply the remainder correction to the last group in order.
records.formula: share( g ) = round_to_currency( converted_base_price( g ) × combo_product_price ÷ total_base_price , document_currency )

rounding.what: Each group's share.
rounding.precision: The document currency's rounding multiple; one hundredth for a currency with two decimal places.
rounding.step: After the multiplication and the division, once per group; the rounding residue is corrected afterwards on the last group.

result.name: share of the choice group
result.stored_or_displayed: carried into the unit price of each child line; the combination product's own line stays at zero

edge_cases.case: One group's base price is zero while others are not.
edge_cases.outcome: That group's share is zero and its child line carries only the chosen item's own supplement.

edge_cases.case: The rounded shares do not add up to the combination product price.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is given to the last choice group in sequence order, so the total is exact.

edge_cases.case: The combination product price is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Every share is zero and the remainder is zero.

edge_cases.case: The division does not terminate.
edge_cases.outcome: The quotient is rounded at the currency's rounding multiple, which is where the residue that the remainder correction absorbs comes from.

worked_examples.description: A menu at fifteen with base prices of eight, three point five zero and two
worked_examples.narrative: Eight multiplied by fifteen divided by thirteen point five zero is eight point eight eight eight eight, rounded to eight point eight nine; the other two groups give three point eight nine and two point two two. The three shares add up to exactly fifteen, so no correction is needed.

worked_examples.description: The same base prices with a menu price of ten
worked_examples.narrative: Each share is again rounded half away from zero at the hundredth, and the three shares happen to add up to the menu price exactly, so the remainder is zero once more.

worked_examples.description: Three equal base prices, which do produce a residue
worked_examples.narrative: One multiplied by ten divided by three is three point three three three three, rounded to three point three three for each of the three groups. Their sum is nine point nine nine, one hundredth short of the menu price, and that hundredth is handed to the last group.

records.name: The prorated share of a choice group when every base price is zero
records.purpose: Shares the combination product's price evenly when no group carries any weight, instead of concentrating the whole price on one group through the remainder correction.

operands.name: combination product price
operands.source: the price the combination product would have had as an ordinary product
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: number of choice groups
operands.source: the combination product
operands.constraints: at least one, since a combination product must hold at least one choice group

preconditions.condition: The total base price is zero, that is every choice group's converted base price is zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The weighted branch applies.

procedure: Divide the combination product price by the number of choice groups.
Round the quotient to the document currency's rounding multiple, half away from zero.
Give every group that same share.
Apply the remainder correction to the last group in order, exactly as in the weighted branch.
records.formula: share( g ) = round_to_currency( combo_product_price ÷ number_of_groups , document_currency )    for every g, when total_base_price = 0

rounding.what: The even share.
rounding.step: After the division, once, and then the remainder is corrected on the last group.

result.name: share of the choice group
result.stored_or_displayed: carried into the unit price of each child line

edge_cases.case: The even division leaves a residue.
edge_cases.outcome: The remainder correction gives it to the last group in sequence order, so the child lines still add up exactly.

edge_cases.case: The combination product price is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Every share is zero and the child lines carry only the item supplements.

edge_cases.case: The combination product holds a single choice group.
edge_cases.outcome: That group takes the whole price.

worked_examples.description: Three groups whose base prices are all zero, with a menu price of ten
worked_examples.narrative: Ten divided by three is three point three three three three, rounded to three point three three for each group. The hundredth left over goes to the last group in sequence order, giving three point three three, three point three three and three point three four, which add up to exactly ten.

records.name: The rounding remainder of the proration
records.purpose: Makes the child lines of a combination product add up to its price exactly, by handing the rounding residue to one determined choice group.

operands.name: combination product price
operands.source: the price to be shared out
operands.constraints: already rounded to the document currency

operands.name: rounded share of each choice group
operands.source: the weighted branch or the even branch of the proration
operands.constraints: each already rounded to the document currency's rounding multiple

operands.name: order of the choice groups
operands.source: the combination product's own groups, ordered by sequence ascending then by identifier
operands.constraints: the last group in that order receives the remainder

preconditions.condition: Every share has already been rounded.
preconditions.otherwise: There would be no residue to correct, and correcting an unrounded share would introduce one.

procedure: Add the rounded shares of every choice group.
Subtract that sum from the combination product price to obtain the remainder.
Add the remainder to the share of the last choice group, taken in sequence ascending then identifier order.
The shares now add up to the combination product price exactly, in the document currency.
records.formula:
remainder = combo_product_price − sum over g of share( g )
share( last_group ) = share( last_group ) + remainder
sum over g of share( g ) = combo_product_price     (exactly, in the document currency)

rounding.what: The residue left by rounding each share.
rounding.method: The remainder is not rounded again; it is the exact difference between two figures already at the currency's precision.
rounding.step: After every share has been rounded and before the child line prices are formed.

result.name: corrected share of the last choice group
result.stored_or_displayed: carried into the unit price of the child line of the last group

edge_cases.case: The rounded shares already add up to the price.
edge_cases.outcome: The remainder is zero and no correction is visible.

edge_cases.case: The rounded shares exceed the price.
edge_cases.outcome: The remainder is negative and the last group's share is reduced by it.

edge_cases.case: There is a single choice group.
edge_cases.outcome: That group is the last one and absorbs any residue, so its share equals the price.

edge_cases.case: Two groups share the same sequence number.
edge_cases.outcome: The identifier breaks the tie, so the group that receives the remainder is determined.

worked_examples.description: A residue of one hundredth over three equal groups
worked_examples.narrative: Ten minus nine point nine nine is one hundredth, which goes to the group of sequence thirty. The three child lines then add up to exactly ten.

worked_examples.description: A proration that needs no correction
worked_examples.narrative: The rounded shares already add up to the menu price, so the correction adds nothing.

records.name: The unit price of the child line of a chosen combination item
records.purpose: Gives each child line of a combination product the price it displays: its group's share of the menu price plus the supplements the chosen item itself carries.

operands.name: share of the item's choice group
operands.source: the proration, after the remainder correction
operands.constraints: already rounded to the document currency

operands.name: extra price of the chosen item
operands.source: the combo item record
operands.constraints: converted into the document currency before being added

operands.name: extra price of the chosen values of attributes that never create variants on that item
operands.source: the configuration chosen on the child line
operands.constraints: converted together with the item's own supplement

operands.name: document currency, document company and document date
operands.unit_or_currency: a currency, a company and a date
operands.source: the document
operands.constraints: the conversion is made at the document date

preconditions.condition: The child line names an item of one of the combination product's choice groups.
preconditions.otherwise: There is no share to attach to and the line is not part of the combination.

procedure: Take the share of the choice group the chosen item belongs to.

Add the item's own extra price and the extra prices of any values of attributes that never create variants chosen on it, both converted from the item's currency into the document currency for the document company at the document date.
Display the total as the child line's unit price.
Note the postcondition: the child lines' unit prices, taken before the per-item supplements, add up to the combination product price exactly.
records.formula: item_unit_price = share( group_of( item ) ) + convert( item_extra_price + no_variant_attributes_price_extra , item_currency , document_currency , document_company , document_date )

rounding.what: The converted supplement.
rounding.step: At the currency conversion of the supplement; the share is already rounded and the addition rounds nothing further.

result.name: unit price of the child line
result.stored_or_displayed: stored as the unit price of the child document line and displayed on the document

edge_cases.case: The chosen item carries no supplement.
edge_cases.outcome: The child line's unit price is its group's share alone.

edge_cases.case: The item's currency differs from the document's.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the supplement is converted; the share is already in the document currency.

edge_cases.case: The item's supplement is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The child line is cheaper than the share; nothing floors the unit price at zero.

edge_cases.case: The buyer chose a value of an attribute that never creates variants on the child line.
edge_cases.outcome: That supplement is converted and added together with the item's own supplement.

worked_examples.description: A lunch menu at fifteen with a steak supplement and a soda supplement
worked_examples.narrative: Each child line takes its group's share and adds the chosen item's supplement: eight point eight nine plus three for the steak, three point eight nine for the salad, two point two two plus zero point five zero for the soda. The order total of eighteen point five zero is the menu price of fifteen plus the three of steak supplement and the fifty hundredths of soda supplement.

records.name: The unit price of the combination product's own line
records.purpose: Fixes the price shown on the line that carries the combination product itself at zero, so that the whole amount is carried by the child lines and each item's revenue, tax and cost land on its own product.

operands.name: combination product price
operands.source: the price shared out over the choice groups
operands.constraints: any amount, including zero

operands.name: shares of the choice groups after the remainder correction
operands.source: the proration
operands.constraints: their sum equals the combination product price exactly

preconditions.condition: The document line carries a combination product and has child lines for the chosen items.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to carry the price and the line prices itself as an ordinary product.

procedure: Set the unit price of the line carrying the combination product to zero.
Leave the whole amount on the child lines, whose shares add up to the combination product price.
Note the consequence for the ledger: each child line names its own product, so revenue, tax and cost of goods sold follow the items rather than the combination.
records.formula:
combo_product_line_unit_price = 0
sum over choice groups of share( group ) = combo_product_price     (exactly, in the document currency)

rounding.what: Nothing on this line; its price is fixed at zero.
rounding.precision: The document currency's rounding multiple applies to the child lines only.

result.name: unit price of the combination product's line
result.stored_or_displayed: stored as the unit price of the parent document line and displayed as zero

edge_cases.case: A discount is displayed by the pricelist rule.
edge_cases.outcome: The larger of the pre-discount base price and the pricelist price is prorated, and the parent line still shows zero.

edge_cases.case: The buyer removes a child line.
edge_cases.outcome: The proration is recomputed over the remaining groups; the parent line stays at zero.

edge_cases.case: The combination product price is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Both the parent line and every child line show zero before item supplements.

worked_examples.description: The lunch menu line and its three child lines
worked_examples.narrative: The parent line shows nothing and the three shares add up to exactly the menu price, which is the invariant the ledger effects of the domain restate.

records.name: The product matrix of a template
records.purpose: Builds the grid in which a user enters quantities for many variants of one template at once, with the first attribute across the columns and every other attribute down the rows.

operands.name: template
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: its valid attribute lines, in their order, define the grid

operands.name: company and target currency
operands.source: the caller; the company defaults to the template's company and failing that to the acting company, and the currency defaults to the template's currency
operands.constraints: used only for the header cells that carry a price

operands.name: flag saying whether extra prices are displayed
operands.source: the caller; supplements are hidden on purchase documents
operands.constraints: when cleared, every header cell reports a supplement of zero

operands.name: active materialised values of each line
operands.source: the template's attribute lines
operands.constraints: in the values' own order

preconditions.condition: The template has at least one valid attribute line.
preconditions.otherwise: There is no first line to spread across the columns and no grid to build.

procedure: Default the company to the template's company and failing that to the acting company, and the currency to the template's currency.
Take the template's valid attribute lines in their order, the active materialised values of the first line in their order, and the identifiers of the active materialised values of every line.
Build the header as a list whose first element is a cell holding the template's display name and whose remaining elements are one header cell per value of the first line.

Build the enumeration: start from a list holding one empty tuple and, for each line's value list in order, replace the enumeration by the list formed by taking each value of that line in order and each partial tuple of the current enumeration in order and appending the value to the tuple, which produces the product in first-line-fastest order.
Cut the enumeration into consecutive chunks of as many entries as there are values on the first line; each chunk is one row.
Build each row's header cell from the members of the row's first entry after the first member, that is from the values every entry of the row shares.

Produce, for each entry of the row, a cell holding the identifiers of the entry sorted ascending under the key `ptav_ids` (product template attribute value identifiers), a quantity of zero under the key `qty` (quantity), and the verdict of the full possibility predicate under the key `is_possible_combination`.
Return the header and the list of rows.
records.formula:
enumeration = fold over lines of ( new_enumeration = [ x + ( y ) for y in values_of_line for x in enumeration ] )
number_of_columns = number_of_values_of_the_first_line
number_of_rows = number_of_entries ÷ number_of_columns
number_of_entries = product over lines of number_of_active_values_of_the_line

rounding.what: Only the amounts carried by the header cells; the grid itself holds no rounded figure.
rounding.precision: The `Product Price` decimal precision for the displayed supplement and the target currency's rounding multiple for its converted amount.
rounding.step: When each header cell's amount is converted, not when the grid is built.

result.name: the header and the rows of the matrix
result.unit_or_currency: cells holding identifiers, a quantity and a verdict, no unit
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed as the entry grid; the quantities the user types are consumed by the calling document, not stored on the matrix

edge_cases.case: The template has a single attribute line.
edge_cases.outcome: There is one row, whose header cell is built from an empty set of values and therefore reads as a single space.

edge_cases.case: A combination is impossible.
edge_cases.outcome: Its cell reports the possibility verdict as false and the client renders it as unavailable rather than as an input box.

edge_cases.case: Supplements are hidden.
edge_cases.outcome: Every header cell reports a supplement of zero and carries neither a currency nor an amount.

edge_cases.case: A line has one active value.
edge_cases.outcome: It multiplies the enumeration by one, so the grid keeps its shape and the value appears in every row header.

worked_examples.description: A two-line template with an exclusion, displayed with supplements
worked_examples.narrative: The enumeration starts from one empty tuple, becomes the three single-value tuples after the size line and the six pairs after the colour line, in first-line-fastest order. Cut into chunks of three, it gives two rows headed by the colours. The bottom-right cell, Size L with Colour White, is marked impossible by the exclusion.

records.name: The name of a matrix header cell
records.purpose: Labels a row or a column of the matrix with the values it stands for, and keeps a row header visible even when it stands for no value at all.

operands.name: set of values the header cell stands for
operands.source: for a column, the single value of the first line; for a row, the members of the row's first entry after the first
operands.constraints: may be empty when the template has a single attribute line

preconditions.condition: The values are taken in the order the entry holds them.
preconditions.otherwise: Two systems could label the same row differently.

procedure: Join the names of the values with a space, a bullet and a space when the set holds at least one value.
Use a single space as the name when the set is empty, so that the client renders a blank row header rather than an empty one, which it would otherwise label as unavailable.
records.formula:
header_cell_name = join_with( " • " , names_of_the_values )     when the set is non-empty
header_cell_name = " "                                          when the set is empty

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is a label.

result.name: header cell name
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed as the row or column label of the matrix

edge_cases.case: The template has a single attribute line.
edge_cases.outcome: The row header stands for no value and reads as a single space.

edge_cases.case: The row stands for two or more values.
edge_cases.outcome: Their names are joined by a bullet with a space on each side, in the order the entry holds them.

edge_cases.case: A value's name is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: It contributes an empty piece to the join, which shows as two separators in a row; nothing corrects this.

worked_examples.description: A row standing for two values and a row standing for none
worked_examples.narrative: Two values are joined by the bullet separator; an empty set gives the single space that keeps the row header blank rather than absent.

records.name: The supplement carried by a matrix header cell and its conversion
records.purpose: Shows, beside a row or column label of the matrix, how much the values it stands for add to the price, converted into the currency the caller asked for.

operands.name: extra price of each value the header cell stands for
operands.source: the Template Attribute Values behind the header cell
operands.constraints: may be zero, positive or negative

operands.name: flag saying whether supplements are displayed
operands.source: the caller; supplements are hidden on purchase documents
operands.constraints: when cleared, the supplement is reported as zero without looking at the values

operands.name: template currency, target currency, company and today's date
operands.unit_or_currency: two currencies, a company and a date
operands.source: the template, the caller and the current day
operands.constraints: the conversion is made at today's date

preconditions.condition: Supplements are displayed.
preconditions.otherwise: The cell's supplement is zero and the cell carries neither a currency nor an amount.

procedure: Sum the extra prices of the values the header cell stands for when supplements are displayed, and take zero otherwise.
Stop when the sum is zero: the cell carries neither the currency nor the amount.
Convert the sum from the template's currency into the target currency, for the company, at today's date, when the sum is not zero.
Carry the target currency and the converted amount on the cell.
records.formula:
header_cell_extra_price = sum_of( price_extra of the values )     when extras are displayed
header_cell_extra_price = 0                                       otherwise
header_cell_price = convert( header_cell_extra_price , from = template_currency , to = target_currency , company = company , date = today )

rounding.what: The converted amount shown on the cell.
rounding.precision: The target currency's rounding multiple, and the `Product Price` decimal precision for display, two digits by default.
rounding.step: At the conversion, after the sum.

result.name: supplement of the header cell, with its currency
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed beside the header cell's name; not stored

edge_cases.case: The sum is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Neither the currency nor the amount appears in the cell.

edge_cases.case: Supplements are hidden, as on a purchase document.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is zero by construction, so no price is ever shown.

edge_cases.case: The row stands for two values that both carry supplements.
edge_cases.outcome: Their supplements are added before the conversion, so the cell shows the whole of what that row adds.

edge_cases.case: The target currency differs from the template's.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion uses today's rate, so the figure shown can change from one day to the next.

worked_examples.description: The header cells of a two-line matrix
worked_examples.narrative: Only the two values with a non-zero supplement carry an amount; the other cells show their name alone, because a zero supplement suppresses both the currency and the price.

records.name: The check digit of a numeric barcode
records.purpose: Computes the last digit of a fixed-length numeric barcode so that any single-digit error and most transpositions are detected; the same arithmetic serves every fixed-length numeric scheme the domain recognises.

operands.name: numeric string whose last character is the check digit position
operands.unit_or_currency: a string of digits, no unit
operands.source: the scanned or composed barcode; the last character may be wrong or a placeholder
operands.constraints: every character before the last must be a digit

operands.name: digits at even positions after reversal
operands.source: the reversed string without its last character, counting positions from zero
operands.constraints: the digit adjacent to the check digit is at position zero and therefore takes the weight three

operands.name: digits at odd positions after reversal
operands.source: the same reversed string
operands.constraints: these take the weight one

preconditions.condition: Every character except the last is a digit.
preconditions.otherwise: The sums cannot be formed and the encoding check that calls this computation reports the string as invalid.

procedure: Drop the last character of the string and reverse what remains, so that the digit adjacent to the check digit is at position zero.
Add the digits at the even positions into the even sum and the digits at the odd positions into the odd sum.
Multiply the even sum by three and add the odd sum to obtain the weighted total.
Take the weighted total modulo ten, subtract that remainder from ten and take the result modulo ten again, which maps a remainder of zero back to a check digit of zero.
Note that reversing first is what makes the arithmetic independent of the length: the digit next to the check digit always carries the weight three, whatever the total length.
records.formula:
weighted_total = even_sum × 3 + odd_sum
check_digit = ( 10 − ( weighted_total mod 10 ) ) mod 10

rounding.what: Nothing; every operand is a whole number and the arithmetic is exact.
rounding.method: None; the final step is a remainder, not a rounding.

result.name: check digit
result.unit_or_currency: a digit from zero to nine, no unit
result.stored_or_displayed: written as the last character of the printed barcode and compared with the last character of a scanned one

edge_cases.case: The weighted total is a multiple of ten.
edge_cases.outcome: The inner remainder is zero, ten minus zero is ten, and the outer remainder maps it back to a check digit of zero.

edge_cases.case: The string is eight, twelve, thirteen, fourteen or eighteen characters long.
edge_cases.outcome: The same arithmetic applies unchanged, which is why one computation serves the eight-digit and thirteen-digit European Article Numbers, the twelve-digit Universal Product Code, the fourteen-digit Global Trade Item Number and the eighteen-digit Serial Shipping Container Code.

edge_cases.case: The last character is a placeholder.
edge_cases.outcome: It is dropped before the arithmetic, so the placeholder never affects the result.

edge_cases.case: The string is shorter than two characters.
edge_cases.outcome: Dropping the last character leaves nothing to sum; both sums are zero, the weighted total is zero and the check digit is zero.

worked_examples.description: The check digit of a twelve-digit weight-embedded prefix
worked_examples.narrative: The digits at the even positions add to thirteen and those at the odd positions to twenty-three; thirteen multiplied by three is thirty-nine, plus twenty-three is sixty-two; sixty-two modulo ten is two, ten minus two is eight, and eight modulo ten is eight.

worked_examples.description: The check digit of a base code whose value field has been blanked
worked_examples.narrative: Eleven multiplied by three is thirty-three, plus seventeen is fifty; fifty modulo ten is zero, ten minus zero is ten and ten modulo ten is zero, so the sanitised base code ends in zero.

worked_examples.description: The check digit of a trade item number padded to eighteen characters
worked_examples.narrative: Forty-three multiplied by three is one hundred and twenty-nine, plus twenty-four is one hundred and fifty-three; one hundred and fifty-three modulo ten is three, ten minus three is seven. The value string ends in seven, so the numeric identifier is accepted.

records.name: The encoding check of a scanned string
records.purpose: Decides whether a scanned string satisfies the fixed-length numeric encoding a barcode rule demands, which is the test that lets the parser skip rules that cannot possibly apply.

operands.name: scanned string
operands.source: the scanner or the caller
operands.constraints: checked character by character

operands.name: encoding name demanded by the rule
operands.source: the barcode rule
operands.constraints: a name outside this set is a configuration error and produces a lookup failure

operands.name: required length of the encoding
operands.source: eight for `ean8` (eight-digit European Article Number), thirteen for `ean13` (thirteen-digit European Article Number), fourteen for `gtin14` (fourteen-digit Global Trade Item Number), twelve for `upca` (twelve-digit Universal Product Code) and eighteen for `sscc` (eighteen-digit Serial Shipping Container Code)
operands.constraints: compared for equality, never as a minimum

preconditions.condition: The encoding name is one of the six the domain recognises.
preconditions.otherwise: The length lookup fails; the configuration that produced the name is at fault.

procedure: Return true at once when the encoding is `any`, whatever the string holds.
Look up the required length for the encoding.

Require that the encoding is not `ean13` or that the first character is not the digit zero, because a thirteen-digit code beginning with zero is a twelve-digit Universal Product Code in disguise and must be treated as one.
Require that the length of the string equals the required length.
Require that every character is a digit.
Require that the check digit computed from the string equals the string's last digit.
Return true only when all four requirements hold, and false otherwise.
records.formula:
encoding_check = ( encoding = any )
  or ( ( encoding ≠ ean13 or first_character ≠ "0" ) and length = required_length and every character is a digit and check_digit( string ) = last_digit )

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is a verdict.

result.name: encoding verdict
result.stored_or_displayed: consumed by the parser to skip a rule; also used when a barcode is validated before storage

edge_cases.case: A thirteen-character numeric string starting with zero is checked against `ean13`.
edge_cases.outcome: False, because such a code is a twelve-digit Universal Product Code carried in thirteen positions.

edge_cases.case: The string carries a letter.
edge_cases.outcome: False, because every character must be a digit.

edge_cases.case: The length is right and the check digit is wrong.
edge_cases.outcome: False; the rule is skipped rather than reported as an error.

edge_cases.case: The rule demands `any`.
edge_cases.outcome: True for every string, including an empty one, so such a rule is always tried.

worked_examples.description: A valid thirteen-digit code and a twelve-digit code presented as thirteen

expected_outputs.reason_string_two: the first character is the digit zero

worked_examples.narrative: The first string is thirteen digits, does not start with zero and ends in the digit the check computation produces, so it passes. The second is refused on the leading zero alone, before its length or its check digit is considered.

records.name: Sanitising a thirteen-digit code
records.purpose: Turns any string into a well-formed thirteen-digit code by truncating or padding it and recomputing its check digit, which is how a base code becomes the value a product lookup can use.

operands.name: input string
operands.source: the base code produced by a pattern match, or a code being stored
operands.constraints: may be shorter or longer than thirteen characters

preconditions.condition: The characters kept after truncation and padding are digits.
preconditions.otherwise: The check digit computation cannot form its sums and the sanitised value is not usable.

procedure: Take the first thirteen characters of the input.
Pad the result on the left with the digit zero until it is thirteen characters long.
Compute the check digit of that padded string.
Replace the last character of the padded string by that check digit.
Return the thirteen-character result.
records.formula: sanitised_thirteen_digit_code = first_thirteen_characters_left_padded_with_zeros_to_thirteen with its last character replaced by check_digit( that padded string )

rounding.what: Nothing; the operation is on characters.

result.name: sanitised thirteen-digit code
result.unit_or_currency: text of thirteen digits, no unit
result.stored_or_displayed: used as the base code of a parse result when the rule's encoding is `ean13`, and as the stored barcode when a code is normalised before storage

edge_cases.case: The input is longer than thirteen characters.
edge_cases.outcome: It is truncated to the first thirteen and the padding step does nothing.

edge_cases.case: The input is shorter than thirteen characters.
edge_cases.outcome: Zeros are added on the left, which preserves the numeric value while fixing the length.

edge_cases.case: The input already ends in the correct check digit.
edge_cases.outcome: The replacement writes the same digit and the value is unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The input is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: Thirteen zeros are formed, whose check digit is zero, so the result is thirteen zeros.

worked_examples.description: Sanitising the base code left by a weight pattern
worked_examples.narrative: The input is already thirteen characters, so nothing is truncated or padded. Its recomputed check digit is zero, which replaces the trailing eight, giving the code a product lookup is performed on.

worked_examples.description: Sanitising a short numeric string
worked_examples.narrative: Eight zeros are added on the left to reach thirteen characters. The last character, five, is dropped and the remaining twelve are reversed, giving four, three, two, one and then eight zeros; the even positions add to six and the odd positions to four, so the weighted total is six multiplied by three plus four, that is twenty-two. Twenty-two modulo ten is two, ten minus two is eight, so the trailing five is replaced by eight.

records.name: Sanitising a twelve-digit code
records.purpose: Produces the twelve-digit form of a code by borrowing the thirteen-digit sanitiser, which is exactly the equivalence between the two numbering schemes.

operands.name: input string
operands.source: the base code produced by a pattern match whose rule demands the twelve-digit Universal Product Code
operands.constraints: may be shorter or longer than twelve characters

preconditions.condition: The characters kept are digits.
preconditions.otherwise: The check digit computation inside the thirteen-digit sanitiser cannot form its sums.

procedure: Prefix the input with the digit zero.
Sanitise the resulting string as a thirteen-digit code, which truncates or pads it and recomputes its check digit.
Remove the leading character of the sanitised thirteen-digit result.
Return the twelve-character remainder.
records.formula: sanitised_twelve_digit_code = sanitised_thirteen_digit_code( "0" followed by the input ) with its leading character removed

rounding.what: Nothing; the operation is on characters.

result.name: sanitised twelve-digit code
result.unit_or_currency: text of twelve digits, no unit
result.stored_or_displayed: used as the base code of a parse result when the rule's encoding is `upca`

edge_cases.case: The input is already twelve digits.
edge_cases.outcome: Prefixing the zero makes thirteen, the check digit is recomputed over the whole thirteen and the zero is stripped again, so only the last digit may change.

edge_cases.case: The input is longer than twelve characters.
edge_cases.outcome: The thirteen-digit step truncates after the prefixed zero, so only the first twelve characters of the input survive.

edge_cases.case: The input is shorter than twelve characters.
edge_cases.outcome: The padding of the thirteen-digit step adds zeros on the left, and one of them is the prefixed zero that is stripped again.

worked_examples.description: Sanitising a twelve-digit base code
worked_examples.narrative: The zero is prefixed, the thirteen-character string is sanitised so that its last digit is the one the check computation produces, and the prefixed zero is stripped, leaving the twelve-digit form.

records.name: Matching a barcode against a rule pattern
records.purpose: Tests a scanned barcode against one rule's pattern and, when the pattern carries a numeric field, extracts the number the label encodes and the base code with that field blanked.

operands.name: barcode string
operands.source: the scan, possibly converted between the twelve-digit and thirteen-digit schemes by the parser
operands.constraints: escaped before use, because it becomes part of the subject of a match against a pattern built partly from itself

operands.name: pattern
operands.source: the barcode rule
operands.constraints: may hold at most one brace group made of letters N for whole digits and letters D for decimal digits

operands.name: whole digits of the value
operands.source: the first characters of the value string, as many as the whole part of the brace group declares
operands.constraints: read as the single digit zero when the whole part is empty

operands.name: decimal digits of the value
operands.source: the value string between the decimal part's start offset and its end offset minus one
operands.constraints: read as the fractional part of a number whose whole part is zero

preconditions.condition: The whole digits extracted are all digits.
preconditions.otherwise: No value is computed and no base code is rewritten; only the plain pattern match decides the verdict.

procedure: Initialise the value to zero, the base code to the barcode and the verdict to false.
Escape the barcode: double every backslash, and put a backslash before every opening brace, every closing brace and every full stop, so that the barcode's own special characters are not interpreted.

Search the pattern for the first group made of an opening brace, then zero or more letters N, then zero or more letters D, then a closing brace, and record its start position and the position one past its closing brace.

Take the value string as the barcode from the start position up to but excluding the end position minus two, the subtraction accounting for the two brace characters that occupy positions in the pattern but not in the barcode.

Find the whole part inside the group, whose length minus two is the number of whole digits, and the decimal part inside the group, whose start and end offsets delimit the decimal digits inside the value string.
Read the whole digits as a whole number, taking zero when they are empty, and the decimal digits as the fractional part.
Add the two to obtain the value, and rewrite the base code by replacing the positions of the numeric field with that many digit-zero characters and then reversing the four escapes in the same order.
Rewrite the pattern likewise, replacing the whole brace group with that many digit-zero characters.
