The rule for the trade item number matches fourteen digits whose check digit agrees, and the separator group matches the empty text because the next character is a digit. The lot rule then consumes seven characters and the separator that follows. The expiry rule reads six digits as the thirty-first of December two thousand and twenty-six, and the remaining string is empty.

worked_examples.description: The four-element label of the standard's own illustration

inputs.scanned_string: the group-separator character, then 01940190976854571033650100138, the group-separator character, then 310200200415131018

worked_examples.narrative: The third record is the interesting one: its rule declares the decimal-usage flag, so the last character of the matched application identifier, two, fixes the decimal position and the six digits read as twenty point zero four kilograms.

worked_examples.description: An alternative encoding that needs no separator
worked_examples.narrative: Placing the fixed-length fields before the variable-length one lets the loop finish without a separator: after the trade item number the string begins with the digits one and seven, which the lot rule cannot match, and after the date the greedy lot match simply reaches the end of the string.

records.name: Unpadding a barcode search under a Global Standards One nomenclature
records.purpose: Rewrites a search on the barcode field so that a fourteen-digit scanned trade item number finds the shorter barcode a product actually stores.

operands.name: search condition set
operands.source: the caller's search
operands.constraints: each condition is rewritten independently

operands.name: list of result types the caller cares about
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: a parsed record whose type is not in the list is skipped

operands.name: name of the field being searched
operands.source: the caller; the barcode field by default
operands.constraints: a condition on another field is left alone

operands.name: suppression flag
operands.source: the context entry `skip_preprocess_gs1` (skip preprocessing for Global Standards One)
operands.constraints: when set, the whole rewrite is skipped

preconditions.condition: The acting company's nomenclature is a Global Standards One nomenclature.
preconditions.otherwise: Every condition is left alone and the search runs as it was written.

preconditions.condition: The suppression flag is not set.
preconditions.otherwise: The rewrite is skipped entirely, which is what the barcode uniqueness check relies on to keep its comparison exact.

procedure: Leave the condition alone when it is not on the named field or when the company's nomenclature is not a Global Standards One nomenclature.
Leave the condition alone when its value is empty.
Rewrite a membership or non-membership comparison over more than one value as the combination with "or" of one equality condition per value, negating the combination for non-membership.
Reduce a membership or non-membership comparison over exactly one value to equality or inequality on that value.
Leave the condition alone when the comparison is none of contains, does-not-contain, equals or differs.
Parse the value as a barcode, an empty parse standing for any parsing or validation failure.
Take the replacing comparison to be contains when the original comparison was contains or equals, and does not contain otherwise.

For each record of the parse in order: skip it when its type is not in the caller's list; return a condition comparing the field to the record's value with the original comparison when its type is `lot`, because lot names are not numeric and must not be unpadded; otherwise return a condition comparing the field to the record's digits without their leading zeros, using the replacing comparison, when the value reads as zero or more leading zeros followed by at least one digit; and stop looking at further records otherwise.

When the parse produced nothing at all, return a condition comparing the field to the digits without the leading zeros using the replacing comparison, but only when the raw value reads as at least one leading zero followed by at least one digit.
Leave the condition alone in every other case.
records.formula:
replacing_comparison = contains       when the original comparison is contains or equals
replacing_comparison = does not contain   otherwise
rewritten_value = record_value with its leading zeros removed     ( parsed record, zero or more leading zeros allowed )
rewritten_value = raw_value with its leading zeros removed        ( no parse, at least one leading zero required )

rounding.what: Nothing; the operation is on text and comparisons.

result.name: rewritten search condition set
result.stored_or_displayed: handed to the search; the rewrite is invisible to the user except in the records that come back

edge_cases.case: The parsed value has no leading zero.
edge_cases.outcome: It is still switched to a contains comparison, which is the difference between the parsed branch and the unparsed one.

edge_cases.case: The raw value has no leading zero and does not parse.
edge_cases.outcome: The condition is left alone, because there is nothing to strip.

edge_cases.case: The parsed record's type is `lot`.
edge_cases.outcome: The original comparison is kept and no zero is stripped, since a lot name may legitimately begin with zeros.

edge_cases.case: The caller needs an exact comparison, as the barcode uniqueness check does.
edge_cases.outcome: It sets the suppression flag, so the search stays exact.

edge_cases.case: A stored thirteen-digit barcode is searched with its fourteen-digit form.
edge_cases.outcome: The unpadded string still has fourteen digits and the product is not found; the rewrite is designed for the opposite direction, where a scan such as fourteen characters with leading zeros unpads to an eight-digit stored barcode.

worked_examples.description: A fourteen-digit scan typed into a product search box
worked_examples.narrative: The scan parses to one product record. Its value matches zero or more leading zeros followed by digits, with none to strip, and the comparison nevertheless becomes contains, which is what lets a stored fourteen-digit barcode be found by a shorter scan and the reverse.

worked_examples.description: A padded scan that finds an eight-digit stored barcode
worked_examples.narrative: With no parse to guide it, the raw value is used: it begins with at least one zero, so the zeros are stripped and the contains comparison finds the product stored with the eight-digit barcode.

records.name: The complete name of a product category
records.purpose: Builds the path a category shows in lists and reports, so that two categories of the same name under different parents can be told apart.

operands.name: name of the category
operands.source: the Product Category
operands.constraints: required

operands.name: complete name of the parent category
operands.source: the parent category, computed the same way
operands.constraints: absent at the root; the hierarchy may hold no cycle

preconditions.condition: The category hierarchy holds no cycle.
preconditions.otherwise: The recursion would not terminate; a cycle is refused when the parent is written.

procedure: Take the parent's complete name when the category has a parent, computed by this same rule.
Join it to the category's own name with a space, a solidus and a space.
Take the category's own name when it has no parent.
Store the result, and recompute it for every descendant when a category is renamed or reparented.
records.formula:
complete_name( category ) = complete_name( parent ) + " / " + name( category )     when a parent exists
complete_name( category ) = name( category )                                        otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is text.

result.name: complete name of the category
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the Product Category and displayed wherever the category appears

edge_cases.case: A category is renamed.
edge_cases.outcome: The complete name of every descendant is rewritten, because the value is stored rather than computed at read time.

edge_cases.case: A category is moved under a new parent.
edge_cases.outcome: Its complete name and those of its descendants are rewritten from the new path.

edge_cases.case: A parent is deleted.
edge_cases.outcome: Its children are deleted with it, so no orphan path remains.

edge_cases.case: The hierarchy would form a cycle.
edge_cases.outcome: The write is refused, which is what keeps the recursion finite.

worked_examples.description: A three-level hierarchy before and after a rename
worked_examples.narrative: Each level appends its own name to its parent's path. Renaming the middle level rewrites both its own complete name and that of its descendant.

records.name: The combination name of a variant
records.purpose: Names the members of a combination that a user needs to see, dropping the ones that carry no information because every variant shares them.

operands.name: members of the combination
operands.source: the variant's stored combination or the configuration chosen by a buyer
operands.constraints: ordered by attribute line then attribute value

operands.name: variant-creation mode of each member's attribute
operands.source: the attribute behind each member
operands.constraints: a member whose attribute never creates variants is removed

operands.name: number of values of each member's line
operands.source: the attribute line, counting active materialised values, or every materialised value when any member of the set is archived
operands.constraints: a line with exactly one such value is a single-value line and its member is removed

preconditions.condition: The activity of every member is known, because the counting rule depends on it.
preconditions.otherwise: An archived variant could lose or gain a member in its name after the line acquired values.

procedure: Remove the members whose attribute never creates variants.
Remove the members that come from a single-value line, counting only active materialised values when every member of the set is active, and counting archived values too when any member is archived.
Join the names of the remaining members with a comma and a space, in the members' own order.
records.formula: combination_name = join_with( ", " , names of the combination members, after removing ( a ) members whose attribute never creates variants and ( b ) members that come from a single-value line )

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is text.

result.name: combination name
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed inside the variant's display name and wherever a chosen configuration is shown

edge_cases.case: Every member is removed.
edge_cases.outcome: The combination name is empty and the variant shows its template's name alone.

edge_cases.case: A line offers one active value and several archived ones, and every member of the set is active.
edge_cases.outcome: It counts as a single-value line and its member is dropped.

edge_cases.case: One member of the set is archived.
edge_cases.outcome: Archived values count towards the line's total, so a line that has since gained values still counts as single-value for that set and the archived variant keeps the name it had.

edge_cases.case: Two members come from lines with the same sequence.
edge_cases.outcome: The value order breaks the tie, so the name is deterministic.

worked_examples.description: A variant before and after a single-value attribute is added
worked_examples.narrative: The material member comes from a line offering one value, so it carries no information and is dropped; the name is unchanged although the variant now holds three members.

worked_examples.description: The same variant after the material line gains a second value
worked_examples.narrative: The line is no longer a single-value line, so its member is kept and the name grows.

records.name: The display name of a variant
records.purpose: Forms the name a variant shows everywhere: the template's name, followed in parentheses by the members that distinguish this variant from its siblings.

operands.name: template name
operands.source: the Product Template
operands.constraints: required

operands.name: combination name
operands.source: the combination name of the variant's members
operands.constraints: may be empty

preconditions.condition: The combination name has already dropped the members that carry no information.
preconditions.otherwise: Every variant of a template with a single-value attribute would show that value, which adds nothing.

procedure: Take the template's name.
Append a space, an opening parenthesis, the combination name and a closing parenthesis when the combination name is not empty.
Use the template's name alone when the combination name is empty.
records.formula:
variant_base_name = template_name                                    when combination_name is empty
variant_base_name = template_name + " (" + combination_name + ")"    otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is text.

result.name: variant display name
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed wherever the variant appears; the vendor-specific display and the internal reference prefix are added on top of it

edge_cases.case: The template has no attribute line.
edge_cases.outcome: The combination name is empty and the variant shows the template's name alone.

edge_cases.case: Every member comes from a single-value line.
edge_cases.outcome: Same as above: no parentheses are shown.

edge_cases.case: The template is renamed.
edge_cases.outcome: Every variant's display name changes with it, because only the template's name is stored.

worked_examples.description: Two variants of the same template
worked_examples.narrative: The first variant shows its two distinguishing members between parentheses; the second, whose members all carry no information, shows the template's name alone.

records.name: The reference of a variant in the context of a partner
records.purpose: Chooses the code to print for a variant on a document addressed to one partner, preferring the code that partner uses over the internal one.

operands.name: internal reference of the variant
operands.source: the Product Variant
operands.constraints: may be unset; internal references are deliberately not unique

operands.name: vendor lines of the variant belonging to the acting companies
operands.source: the variant's vendor price lines
operands.constraints: walked in their own order; only readable when the reader may read vendor price lines

operands.name: context partner
operands.source: the document or the caller
operands.constraints: a line whose partner differs is not considered

operands.name: vendor product code of each line
operands.source: the vendor line
operands.constraints: may be unset, in which case the reference falls back to the internal one

preconditions.condition: The reader may read vendor price lines.
preconditions.otherwise: The walk is skipped and the internal reference stands.

procedure: Start from the variant's internal reference.
Walk the variant's vendor lines that belong to the acting companies, in their own order, considering only the lines whose partner is the context partner.
Skip a line that names a different variant.
Set the reference to the line's vendor product code when it has one, and back to the internal reference when it has none.
Stop walking as soon as a line that names this exact variant has been used.
Return the reference reached, so that a variant-specific vendor line wins over a template-wide one and the last template-wide line of that partner wins over the earlier ones.
records.formula:
reference = internal_reference
for each vendor line L of this partner, in order:  reference = L.vendor_product_code when set, else internal_reference ;  stop when L names this exact variant

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is text.

result.name: reference of the variant for that partner
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed on documents addressed to the partner and used as the bracketed prefix of the display name

edge_cases.case: No vendor line names the partner.
edge_cases.outcome: The internal reference stands.

edge_cases.case: Two template-wide lines name the partner.
edge_cases.outcome: The walk does not stop on either, so the last one wins.

edge_cases.case: A variant-specific line and a template-wide line both name the partner.
edge_cases.outcome: The walk stops on the variant-specific one, whichever order they are in, because a line that names this exact variant ends the walk.

edge_cases.case: The winning line carries no vendor product code.
edge_cases.outcome: The reference falls back to the internal reference, so an empty code does not blank the document.

worked_examples.description: Two template-wide lines followed by a variant-specific one
worked_examples.narrative: Each matching line overwrites the reference, so the last template-wide line beats the first; the variant-specific line both overwrites and ends the walk.

records.name: The customer reference of a variant
records.purpose: Chooses the label a variant shows to one partner, using the name that partner knows the product by when there is one.

operands.name: vendor lines whose partner matches the context partner
operands.source: the variant's vendor price lines
operands.constraints: only the first matching line is used

operands.name: vendor product name of that line
operands.source: the vendor line
operands.constraints: may be unset

operands.name: internal reference and product name
operands.source: the variant
operands.constraints: used as successive fallbacks

preconditions.condition: A partner is named in the context.
preconditions.otherwise: The plain display name is returned.

procedure: Find the first vendor line whose partner matches the context partner.
Take that line's vendor product name, or failing that the internal reference, or failing that the product's name.
Prefix the chosen text with the reference between brackets when there is a reference.
Return the plain display name when no vendor line matches.
records.formula:
customer_reference = "[" + reference + "] " + ( vendor_product_name or internal_reference or product_name )   when a vendor line of that partner exists and a reference exists
customer_reference = vendor_product_name or internal_reference or product_name                                     when a vendor line exists and no reference does
customer_reference = display_name                                                                                  when no vendor line matches

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is text.

result.name: customer reference of the variant
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed on documents addressed to that partner

edge_cases.case: The matching vendor line carries no product name.
edge_cases.outcome: The internal reference is used, and the product's name when there is no internal reference either.

edge_cases.case: No vendor line names the partner.
edge_cases.outcome: The plain display name of the variant is used.

edge_cases.case: There is a reference to prefix.
edge_cases.outcome: It is shown between brackets before the chosen text, which is the form a user may paste back into a search box.

worked_examples.description: A partner who knows the product by another name

inputs.context_partner: the vendor of the first line

worked_examples.narrative: The vendor's own name for the product wins over the internal one, and the reference chosen for that partner is shown between brackets in front of it.

records.name: Searching for a product by name
records.purpose: Finds the record a user means when they type or scan something, going from the most specific match to the least so that a code finds one product rather than a hundred.

operands.name: search term
operands.source: the user or the scanner
operands.constraints: an empty term falls back to the framework's default search

operands.name: comparison asked for
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: the staged search applies to equals, contains, contains-with-wildcards, matches and matches-with-wildcards, and has its own branch for negative comparisons

operands.name: result limit
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: the name stage runs only while the limit has not been reached

operands.name: context partner
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: enables the vendor-line stage

preconditions.condition: The search term is not empty.
preconditions.otherwise: The framework's default name search runs instead.

procedure: Search on internal reference exactly equal to the term when the comparison is equals, contains, contains-with-wildcards, matches or matches-with-wildcards, and then, when that finds nothing, on barcode exactly equal to the term.

When nothing was found and the comparison is positive, search on internal reference with the caller's comparison, and then, while the limit has not been reached, on name with the caller's comparison excluding the identifiers already found; the two searches are kept separate deliberately, because combining them with "or" is markedly slower on a large catalogue.
When nothing was found and the comparison is negative, search for records whose name satisfies the negative comparison and whose internal reference either satisfies it or is unset.
When nothing was found, the comparison is positive and the term carries a bracketed section, search on internal reference exactly equal to the text inside the first pair of brackets.
When nothing was found and a partner is named in the context, search the vendor lines of that partner whose vendor product code or vendor product name satisfies the comparison.
Return the identifiers and display names of what was found, read as a privileged reader so that vendor-derived display names are complete.
records.formula:
stage 1 = internal_reference = term , then barcode = term
stage 2 = internal_reference ⋈ term , then name ⋈ term excluding the identifiers already found
stage 3 = name ⋈ term and ( internal_reference ⋈ term or internal_reference unset )     for a negative comparison
stage 4 = internal_reference = text inside the first pair of brackets
stage 5 = vendor_product_code ⋈ term or vendor_product_name ⋈ term , for the context partner

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is a list of records.

result.name: identifiers and display names of the matching products
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed in the search box; the display names are read as a privileged reader

edge_cases.case: The term is a barcode that also matches many names.
edge_cases.outcome: The exact barcode stage returns the single product and the later stages never run.

edge_cases.case: The term is a whole display name such as a bracketed reference followed by a product name.
edge_cases.outcome: The bracket stage finds the product by the text inside the first pair of brackets.

edge_cases.case: The comparison is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The dedicated stage requires the name to satisfy it and the internal reference to satisfy it or be unset, so a product with no reference is not excluded by accident.

edge_cases.case: The limit is reached by the internal reference stage.
edge_cases.outcome: The name stage does not run, so a caller asking for few results gets the more specific ones.

edge_cases.case: A partner is in the context and nothing else matched.
edge_cases.outcome: The vendor lines of that partner are searched on both the vendor product code and the vendor product name.

worked_examples.description: Pasting a complete display name into the search box
worked_examples.narrative: No internal reference and no barcode equals the whole pasted text, and no product name contains it either, so the bracket stage extracts the reference between the first pair of brackets and finds the one product.

worked_examples.description: Scanning a barcode into the search box
worked_examples.narrative: The exact barcode stage finds the single product, so the broader stages that would have matched many names never run.

records.name: The display-name search condition used by generic searches
records.purpose: Widens a generic search on the display name of a product to every field a user might have typed, and combines the parts differently for a positive and a negative comparison.

operands.name: search term or list of terms
operands.unit_or_currency: text or a list of texts, no unit
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: a membership comparison carries a list

operands.name: comparison asked for
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: positive comparisons take the union of the parts; negative comparisons take the conjunction of the individual negative conditions

operands.name: context partner
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: enables the vendor product code and vendor product name parts

preconditions.condition: The comparison is one the widening supports.
preconditions.otherwise: The barcode part is left out, since it takes part only for membership comparisons and positive contains-style comparisons.

procedure: Match on the template name.
Match on the internal reference.
Match on the barcode, for membership comparisons and for positive contains-style comparisons.
Match on the text inside the brackets of each membership value.
Match on the vendor product code and the vendor product name when a partner is named in the context.
Take the union of the separate searches for a positive comparison, and the conjunction of the individual negative conditions for a negative one.
records.formula:
positive_condition = template_name ⋈ term  or  internal_reference ⋈ term  or  barcode ⋈ term  or  internal_reference = bracketed_text  or  vendor_product_code ⋈ term  or  vendor_product_name ⋈ term
negative_condition = template_name ⋈ term  and  internal_reference ⋈ term  and  ( the other parts, each negated )

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is a search condition.

result.name: display-name search condition
result.stored_or_displayed: handed to the search; not stored

edge_cases.case: The comparison is a membership over several values.
edge_cases.outcome: The barcode part takes part, and the bracketed text of each value is matched too.

edge_cases.case: The comparison is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: Each part becomes a negative condition and they are joined with "and", so a record is kept only when it fails every part.

edge_cases.case: No partner is in the context.
edge_cases.outcome: The vendor parts are left out.

edge_cases.case: Under a Global Standards One nomenclature.
edge_cases.outcome: The barcode part is rewritten by the unpadding preprocessing before the search runs, unless the suppression flag is set.

worked_examples.description: A positive generic search with a partner in the context
worked_examples.narrative: Each part is searched separately and the identifiers found are added together, which is faster on a large catalogue than one combined condition.

worked_examples.description: A negative generic search
worked_examples.narrative: For a negative comparison the parts are joined with "and", so a product is returned only when neither its name nor its internal reference carries the term.

records.name: The zoomability flag of a product image
records.purpose: Decides whether a storefront may offer a zoom on a product image, which is worth doing only when the original carries more detail than the derivative shown.

operands.name: original image
operands.source: the variant when it has its own image, and the template otherwise
operands.constraints: must exist for the flag to be true

operands.name: size in pixels of the original image and of the one-thousand-and-twenty-four-pixel derivative
operands.source: the stored images, with their contents actually loaded
operands.constraints: compared strictly; the contents must be loaded rather than substituted by their size

preconditions.condition: The image contents are loaded rather than replaced by their byte size.
preconditions.otherwise: The comparison would be made between two sizes in bytes and would answer a different question.

procedure: Check that the original image exists.
Compare the original's size in pixels with that of the one-thousand-and-twenty-four-pixel derivative.
Set the flag when the original is strictly larger.
On a variant, use the variant's own images when the variant has its own image, and the template's otherwise.
records.formula: can_image_1024_be_zoomed = ( the original image exists ) and ( the original image is strictly larger, in pixels, than the one-thousand-and-twenty-four-pixel derivative )

rounding.what: Nothing; the comparison is between whole pixel counts.

result.name: zoomability flag
result.stored_or_displayed: computed and displayed to the storefront, which offers a zoom only when it is true

edge_cases.case: The original is exactly the size of the derivative.
edge_cases.outcome: False, because the comparison is strict and a zoom would show nothing new.

edge_cases.case: No original image exists.
edge_cases.outcome: False.

edge_cases.case: The variant has no image of its own.
edge_cases.outcome: The template's images decide the flag.

worked_examples.description: Two products, one with a large original and one with a small one
worked_examples.narrative: The first original is strictly larger than its derivative, so a zoom reveals more detail. The second is the same size, so the flag is false.

records.name: The four day counts of a product and the four dates they produce
records.purpose: States which of a product's day counts is measured forwards from a receipt and which are measured backwards from the expiration date, which is the arithmetic every expiry date on a lot rests on.

operands.name: expiration day count
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: added to the receipt moment; the only count measured forwards

operands.name: best-before day count
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: subtracted from the expiration date

operands.name: removal day count
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: subtracted from the expiration date

operands.name: alert day count
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: subtracted from the expiration date

preconditions.condition: The product uses expiration dates.
preconditions.otherwise: None of the four dates is computed, and the three derived dates are cleared on the lot.

procedure: Add the expiration day count to the receipt moment to obtain the expiration date.
Subtract the best-before day count from the expiration date to obtain the best-before date.
Subtract the removal day count from the expiration date to obtain the removal date.
Subtract the alert day count from the expiration date to obtain the alert date.
Keep the time of day of the moment the arithmetic starts from, since whole days are added and subtracted.
records.formula:
expiration_date = receipt_moment + expiration_day_count days
best_before_date = expiration_date − best_before_day_count days
removal_date     = expiration_date − removal_day_count days
alert_date       = expiration_date − alert_day_count days

rounding.what: Nothing; whole days are added to or subtracted from a moment.
rounding.precision: Whole days; the time of day is preserved.

result.name: the four dates of a lot
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the lot as its expiration date, best-before date, removal date and alert date

edge_cases.case: A day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The date it governs equals the expiration date, or the receipt moment in the case of the expiration day count.

edge_cases.case: A day count is larger than the expiration day count.
edge_cases.outcome: The derived date falls before the receipt, which is allowed; nothing clamps it.

edge_cases.case: The product stops using expiration dates.
edge_cases.outcome: The expiration date is cleared and the three derived dates are cleared with it.

edge_cases.case: The arithmetic crosses a change of civil time.
edge_cases.outcome: Whole days are added to a moment, so the stored time of day is preserved as it stands.

worked_examples.description: A yoghurt with four day counts, received at a stated moment
worked_examples.narrative: Thirty days after the receipt gives the expiration date; five, three and ten days before it give the best-before, removal and alert dates, each keeping the time of day of half past nine in the morning.

records.name: Computing the expiration date of a lot
records.purpose: Gives a newly created lot the expiration date its product implies, while leaving a date a user has already set alone.

operands.name: current moment
operands.source: the server's current local moment at the instant of the computation
operands.constraints: not a date-only value; the resulting expiration date carries a time of day

operands.name: expiration day count
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: flag saying whether the product uses expiration dates
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: the computation runs only when it is set

operands.name: expiration date already on the lot
operands.source: the lot
operands.constraints: when set, it is left as it is

preconditions.condition: The product uses expiration dates and the lot has no expiration date yet.
preconditions.otherwise: The field is cleared when the product does not use expiration dates, and left untouched when the lot already carries a date.

procedure: Clear the expiration date when the product does not use expiration dates.
Leave the expiration date alone when the lot already carries one.
Otherwise add the expiration day count, in whole days, to the server's current local moment.
Store the result, which carries the time of day of that moment.
Allow a user to overwrite the stored value afterwards.
records.formula:
expiration_date = current_moment + expiration_day_count days     when the product uses expiration dates and the lot has none
expiration_date = cleared                                          when the product does not use expiration dates

rounding.what: Nothing; whole days are added to a moment.
rounding.precision: Whole days; the time of day of the current moment is preserved.

result.name: expiration date of the lot
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the lot; may be overwritten by a user and by the shift branch of the derived dates

edge_cases.case: The expiration day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The expiration date is the current moment itself, so the expiry alert flag becomes true immediately afterwards.

edge_cases.case: The lot already has an expiration date.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is computed, which is what lets an import or a certificate set the date.

edge_cases.case: The product stops using expiration dates.
edge_cases.outcome: The field is cleared and the three derived dates are cleared as well.

worked_examples.description: A lot created by a receipt of yoghurt
worked_examples.narrative: Thirty whole days after half past nine on the eleventh of September is half past nine on the eleventh of October; the time of day is carried over unchanged.

records.name: The three derived dates of a lot, initialisation branch
records.purpose: Sets the best-before, removal and alert dates from the product's day counts when a lot is first given an expiration date or when its product changes.

operands.name: expiration date of the lot
operands.source: the lot
operands.constraints: must be set for this branch to run

operands.name: best-before, removal and alert day counts
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: each subtracted from the expiration date

operands.name: previous stored state of the lot
operands.source: the lot before the write
operands.constraints: used to decide which branch applies

preconditions.condition: The product uses expiration dates and the lot has an expiration date.
preconditions.otherwise: The three dates are cleared when the product does not use expiration dates, and left untouched when the lot has no expiration date.

preconditions.condition: The product has changed since the last stored state, or none of the three derived dates is set, or the expiration date has just been set where there was none before.
preconditions.otherwise: The shift branch applies instead.

procedure: Clear the three derived dates when the product does not use expiration dates, and stop.
Leave the three derived dates untouched when the lot has no expiration date, and stop.
Subtract the best-before day count from the expiration date and store the result as the best-before date.
Subtract the removal day count from the expiration date and store the result as the removal date.
Subtract the alert day count from the expiration date and store the result as the alert date.
records.formula:
best_before_date = expiration_date − best_before_day_count days
removal_date     = expiration_date − removal_day_count days
alert_date       = expiration_date − alert_day_count days

rounding.what: Nothing; whole days are subtracted from a moment.
rounding.precision: Whole days; the time of day of the expiration date is preserved.

result.name: the best-before date, the removal date and the alert date
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the lot

edge_cases.case: A day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: That date equals the expiration date.

edge_cases.case: The product of the lot is changed.
edge_cases.outcome: The branch runs again from the new product's day counts, so any manual adjustment is lost.

edge_cases.case: None of the three dates is set although the expiration date is.
edge_cases.outcome: The branch runs, which is how an imported lot acquires its derived dates.

edge_cases.case: The product stops using expiration dates.
edge_cases.outcome: All three dates are cleared.

worked_examples.description: A newly created lot of yoghurt
worked_examples.narrative: The product has just been set, so the initialisation branch applies and each date is the expiration date less its own day count, keeping the time of day.

records.name: The three derived dates of a lot, shift branch
records.purpose: Moves the best-before, removal and alert dates by the same amount as a change of expiration date, so that a manual adjustment made by a warehouse keeps its relative position.

operands.name: new expiration date
operands.source: the write being applied to the lot
operands.constraints: must be set

operands.name: previous expiration date
operands.source: the lot before the write
operands.constraints: must have been set for this branch to apply

operands.name: previous best-before, removal and alert dates
operands.source: the lot before the write
operands.constraints: a date that was empty stays empty

preconditions.condition: The expiration date is being changed and there was a previous expiration date.
preconditions.otherwise: The initialisation branch applies.

procedure: Compute the shift as the new expiration date less the previous one.
Add the shift to the previous best-before date, but only when that date was set.
Add the shift to the previous removal date, but only when that date was set.
Add the shift to the previous alert date, but only when that date was set.
Leave any of the three that was empty empty.
records.formula:
shift            = new_expiration_date − previous_expiration_date
best_before_date = previous_best_before_date + shift      ( only when it was set )
removal_date     = previous_removal_date     + shift      ( only when it was set )
alert_date       = previous_alert_date       + shift      ( only when it was set )

rounding.what: Nothing; a difference between two moments is added to a moment.
rounding.precision: The shift is exact, down to the time of day.

result.name: the shifted best-before, removal and alert dates
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the lot

edge_cases.case: A derived date was empty.
edge_cases.outcome: It stays empty; the shift is not applied to nothing.

edge_cases.case: The new expiration date is earlier than the previous one.
edge_cases.outcome: The shift is negative and every derived date moves earlier by the same amount.

edge_cases.case: A user had tightened one of the derived dates.
edge_cases.outcome: The adjustment is preserved, because the shift keeps the distance the user chose rather than recomputing it from the product's day count.

edge_cases.case: The product changes in the same write.
edge_cases.outcome: The initialisation branch applies instead, and the manual adjustment is lost.

worked_examples.description: A supplier certificate extending the shelf life of a lot whose removal date had been tightened
worked_examples.narrative: The inspector had moved the removal date from the eighth to the seventh of October, four days before expiry instead of the product's three. Extending the expiration by ten days moves every derived date by ten days, so the removal date stays four days before expiry rather than reverting to three.

records.name: The expiry alert flag of a lot
records.purpose: Marks a lot as expired, which is what makes a delivery of that lot ask for confirmation and what shows the lot on the expiry lists.

operands.name: expiration date of the lot
operands.source: the lot
operands.constraints: may be unset

operands.name: current moment
operands.source: the instant the flag is evaluated
operands.constraints: compared including the time of day

preconditions.condition: The lot carries an expiration date.
preconditions.otherwise: The flag is false, whatever the current moment.

procedure: Check that the lot has an expiration date.
Compare that date with the current moment.
Set the flag when the expiration date is at or before the current moment, and clear it otherwise.
records.formula: expiry_alert = ( expiration_date exists ) and ( expiration_date ≤ current_moment )

rounding.what: Nothing; two moments are compared, time of day included.

result.name: expiry alert flag
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed on the lot and used by the delivery confirmation of the inventory domain

edge_cases.case: The current moment equals the expiration date exactly.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is true, because the comparison includes equality.

edge_cases.case: The lot has no expiration date.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is false.

edge_cases.case: The expiration date is extended after the flag became true.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag becomes false again at once, since it is evaluated from the stored date and the current moment.

worked_examples.description: The same lot evaluated before and after its expiry, with the original and the extended date
worked_examples.narrative: One minute after half past nine on the eleventh of October the original date has passed and the flag is true. With the extended date the flag stays false until exactly half past nine on the twenty-first, when equality makes it true.

records.name: The availability of a stock quantity past its removal date
records.purpose: Stops goods counting as available for new reservations from their removal date onwards, which is how expiring stock is kept out of the ordinary picking flow.

operands.name: removal date of the stock quantity record
operands.source: the quantity record, which takes it from its lot
operands.constraints: may be unset

operands.name: current moment
operands.source: the instant availability is evaluated
operands.constraints: compared including the time of day

operands.name: flag saying whether the product uses expiration dates
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: the zeroing applies only when it is set

preconditions.condition: The product uses expiration dates and the quantity record carries a removal date.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary available-quantity computation of the inventory operations domain applies unchanged.

procedure: Check that the product uses expiration dates.
Check that the quantity record has a removal date.
Report an available quantity of zero when that removal date is at or before the current moment.
Fall back to the ordinary available-quantity computation of the inventory operations domain otherwise.
records.formula:
available_quantity( quant ) = 0    when the product uses expiration dates and the quant's removal date exists and the quant's removal date ≤ current_moment
available_quantity( quant ) = the ordinary available-quantity formula    otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing at this step; the ordinary computation applies its own unit rounding when this branch does not fire.
rounding.precision: The comparison is to the instant; the quantity is expressed in the product's unit of measure.

result.name: available quantity of the stock quantity record
result.stored_or_displayed: computed and displayed on the quantity record; consumed by reservation

edge_cases.case: The current moment equals the removal date.
edge_cases.outcome: The quantity stops being available, because the comparison includes equality.

edge_cases.case: The quantity record has no removal date.
edge_cases.outcome: The ordinary computation applies, so untracked goods are unaffected.

edge_cases.case: The removal date is shifted later by a change of expiration date.
edge_cases.outcome: The goods become available again from that moment on.

edge_cases.case: Goods are already reserved when the removal date passes.
edge_cases.outcome: Only new reservations are affected; the availability figure is what falls to zero.

worked_examples.description: A lot of yoghurt whose removal date has been shifted
worked_examples.narrative: One minute before the removal date the twenty-four units are available; one minute after it the available quantity is zero although the goods are still physically on hand.

records.name: The expiration date of a move line
records.purpose: Gives a line of a goods movement its own expiration date, because the lot the line will create may not exist yet when the line is prepared.

operands.name: expiration date of the line's lot
operands.source: the lot of the line's quantity record, or the lot named on the line
operands.constraints: takes precedence over every other source

operands.name: scheduled moment of the transfer
operands.source: the transfer the line belongs to; today's date when the transfer has none
operands.constraints: used only when the operation type creates lots

operands.name: expiration day count
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: added to the scheduled moment

operands.name: flags: whether the operation type creates lots and whether the product uses expiration dates
operands.source: the operation type and the product
operands.constraints: both govern which branch applies

preconditions.condition: The line names no lot and no quantity record with a lot.
preconditions.otherwise: The lot's own expiration date is taken and no arithmetic is performed.

procedure: Take the expiration date of the lot when the line's quantity record has a lot or the line names one.

Otherwise, when the line's operation type creates lots and the product uses expiration dates, add the expiration day count to the transfer's scheduled moment, or to today when the transfer has none, but only when the line has no expiration date yet.
Otherwise, when the line's operation type creates lots and the product does not use expiration dates, empty the line's expiration date.
Copy the line's expiration date onto the lot when the line eventually creates it.
records.formula:
line_expiration_date = lot_expiration_date                                                              when a lot is known
line_expiration_date = ( transfer_scheduled_moment or today ) + expiration_day_count days              when the operation type creates lots, the product uses expiration dates and the line has none yet
line_expiration_date = empty                                                                           when the operation type creates lots and the product does not use expiration dates

rounding.what: Nothing; whole days are added to a moment.
rounding.precision: Whole days; the time of day of the scheduled moment is preserved.

result.name: expiration date of the move line
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the move line and copied onto the lot the line creates

edge_cases.case: The line already carries an expiration date.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not overwritten by the arithmetic branch.

edge_cases.case: The transfer has no scheduled moment.
edge_cases.outcome: Today's date is used as the base.

edge_cases.case: The operation type does not create lots.
edge_cases.outcome: Neither branch fires and the line keeps whatever it has.

edge_cases.case: The lot is known but has no expiration date.
edge_cases.outcome: The line's expiration date is that empty value; the arithmetic branch is not reached, because a lot is known.

worked_examples.description: A receipt line prepared before its lot exists
worked_examples.narrative: No lot is known, the operation type creates lots and the product uses expiration dates, so thirty days are added to the transfer's scheduled moment; the value is copied onto the lot when the line creates it.

records.name: The removal date of a move line
records.purpose: Gives a line of a goods movement the removal date the goods it will create carry, so that the first-expiry ordering can use it before the lot exists.

operands.name: removal date of the line's lot
operands.source: the lot named on the line
operands.constraints: takes precedence over the arithmetic

operands.name: expiration date of the line
operands.source: the move line, computed by its own rule
operands.constraints: must be set for the arithmetic branch

operands.name: removal day count
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: subtracted from the line's expiration date

operands.name: flags: whether the operation type creates lots and whether the product uses expiration dates
operands.source: the operation type and the product
operands.constraints: both govern which branch applies

preconditions.condition: The line's lot carries no removal date.
preconditions.otherwise: That date is taken and no arithmetic is performed.

procedure: Take the lot's removal date when the line's lot has one.
Otherwise, when the line's operation type creates lots, the product uses expiration dates and the line has an expiration date, subtract the removal day count from the line's expiration date.
Otherwise, when the operation type creates lots and either the product does not use expiration dates or the line has no expiration date, empty the line's removal date.
records.formula:
line_removal_date = lot_removal_date                                        when the lot has one
line_removal_date = line_expiration_date − removal_day_count days           when the operation type creates lots, the product uses expiration dates and the line has an expiration date
line_removal_date = empty                                                   otherwise, when the operation type creates lots

rounding.what: Nothing; whole days are subtracted from a moment.
rounding.precision: Whole days; the time of day is preserved.

result.name: removal date of the move line
result.stored_or_displayed: stored on the move line and used by the first-expiry ordering

edge_cases.case: The line has no expiration date.
edge_cases.outcome: The removal date is emptied, because the arithmetic has nothing to subtract from.

edge_cases.case: The removal day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The removal date equals the line's expiration date.

edge_cases.case: The lot exists and carries a removal date a user has adjusted.
edge_cases.outcome: That adjusted date is used, not the product's default.

worked_examples.description: The removal date of the same receipt line
worked_examples.narrative: Three whole days before half past nine on the eleventh of October is half past nine on the eighth.

records.name: The default expiration date of a generated batch of lot lines
records.purpose: Fills the expiration date of every line a user generates in one run of serial numbers on a movement, using the movement's own schedule as the base.

operands.name: scheduled moment of the transfer
operands.source: the transfer; today's date when the transfer has none
operands.constraints: the base of the arithmetic

operands.name: expiration day count
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: added to the base

operands.name: value already present in the prepared line
operands.source: the prepared line values
operands.constraints: never overwritten

preconditions.condition: The prepared line carries no expiration date yet.
preconditions.otherwise: The value already present is kept, so a user's own entry survives the generation.

procedure: Take the transfer's scheduled moment, or today's date when the transfer has none.
Add the expiration day count in whole days.
Write the result as the default expiration date of each generated line.
Never overwrite a value already present in a prepared line.
records.formula: default_expiration_date = ( transfer_scheduled_moment or today ) + expiration_day_count days

rounding.what: Nothing; whole days are added to a moment.
rounding.precision: Whole days; the time of day of the base is preserved.

result.name: default expiration date of each generated line
result.stored_or_displayed: written onto the generated move lines and copied onto the lots they create

edge_cases.case: The transfer has no scheduled moment.
edge_cases.outcome: Today's date is the base.

edge_cases.case: The prepared line already carries an expiration date.
edge_cases.outcome: It is kept unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The expiration day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The default date is the base itself.

worked_examples.description: Generating ten serial numbers on a scheduled receipt
worked_examples.narrative: Every generated line receives the same default, thirty days after the transfer's scheduled moment.

records.name: The default expiration date of the serial-number command generator
records.purpose: Fills the expiration date when serial numbers are generated by the command generator rather than from a movement, where the base is the current day rather than a schedule.

operands.name: today's date
operands.source: the current day
operands.constraints: the base of the arithmetic, in place of the transfer's scheduled moment

operands.name: expiration day count
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: added to the base

operands.name: value already present in the prepared line
operands.source: the prepared line values
operands.constraints: never overwritten

preconditions.condition: The prepared line carries no expiration date yet.
preconditions.otherwise: The value already present is kept.

procedure: Take today's date as the base, whatever the transfer's schedule says.
Add the expiration day count in whole days.
Write the result as the default expiration date of each generated line.
Never overwrite a value already present in a prepared line.
records.formula: default_expiration_date = today + expiration_day_count days

rounding.what: Nothing; whole days are added to a date.

result.name: default expiration date of each generated line
result.stored_or_displayed: written onto the generated lines

edge_cases.case: The transfer carries a scheduled moment in the future.
edge_cases.outcome: It is ignored by this generator, which is the difference between the two variants of the computation.

edge_cases.case: The prepared line already carries a date.
edge_cases.outcome: It is kept unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The expiration day count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The default date is today.

worked_examples.description: The command generator run on a day earlier than the transfer's schedule
worked_examples.narrative: The generator adds the thirty days to today rather than to the transfer's schedule, so the date differs by a week from what the movement-driven generation would have produced.

records.name: Reading a typed date out of free text
records.purpose: Decides whether the first number of a scanned or typed string is a day, a month or a year, so that a barcode-driven screen can accept a date it cannot otherwise classify.

operands.name: components of the string
operands.source: the string split on hyphens, solidi and spaces
operands.constraints: only the first two components are examined

operands.name: reader's language date format
operands.source: the reader's language
operands.constraints: consulted only when the string is ambiguous

operands.name: flag saying whether the move's product uses expiration dates
operands.source: the product of the move
operands.constraints: when cleared, the string is ignored rather than rejected

preconditions.condition: The screen could not classify the string in any other way.
preconditions.otherwise: The other classification wins and no date reading is attempted.

preconditions.condition: The move's product uses expiration dates.
preconditions.otherwise: The string is ignored rather than rejected, and nothing is written.

procedure: Split the string on hyphens, solidi and spaces and take the first two components.
Infer no option from this string and try the next one when fewer than two components are found.
Set no option and stop when the first component carries a letter, because it is a month name and month-first is the default reading.
Set year-first and stop when the first component read as a number is greater than thirty-one, because it must be a year.
Set day-first and stop when the first component read as a number is greater than twelve and the second either carries a letter or is at most twelve, because the first must be a day.

Otherwise fall back to the reader's language date format: return at once with nothing set when it begins with a month placeholder, set day-first and stop when it begins with a day placeholder, and set year-first and stop when it begins with a year placeholder.
Write the resulting date as the line's expiration date when a date could be read.
records.formula:
first component carries a letter        ⇒ month first ( nothing set )
first component > 31                    ⇒ year first
first component > 12 and ( second component carries a letter or second component ≤ 12 ) ⇒ day first
otherwise                               ⇒ follow the reader's language date format

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is a date and an ordering option.

result.name: the expiration date read from the string, and the ordering option used to read it
result.stored_or_displayed: written as the expiration date of the move line

edge_cases.case: The string carries only one component.
edge_cases.outcome: No option is inferred from it and the next string is tried.

edge_cases.case: Both of the first two numbers are at most twelve.
edge_cases.outcome: The string is ambiguous and the reader's language date format decides.

edge_cases.case: The move's product does not use expiration dates.
edge_cases.outcome: The string is ignored rather than rejected, so a scan that happens to look like a date does not stop the operator.

edge_cases.case: The first component is a month name.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is set, because month-first is already the default reading.

worked_examples.description: Three strings classified by the first two components
worked_examples.narrative: The first string begins with a number greater than thirty-one, so it is a year. The second begins with twenty-five, greater than twelve, and its second component is at most twelve, so the first is a day. The third is ambiguous, both numbers being at most twelve, so the reader's language decides and the day is read first.

records.name: The expiry reminder
records.purpose: Raises one activity per lot whose alert date has been reached and that still holds stock inside the company, and marks every selected lot so that it is never reminded twice.

operands.name: alert date of each lot
operands.source: the lot
operands.constraints: compared with today's date

operands.name: reminded flag of each lot
operands.source: the lot
operands.constraints: only lots whose flag is false are selected

operands.name: stock quantity records of the lot
operands.unit_or_currency: quantities in the product's unit of measure
operands.source: the quantity records of the lot
operands.constraints: at least one strictly positive quantity in a location whose usage is internal is required for an activity

operands.name: responsible user of the product
operands.source: the product, as seen from the lot's company; failing that the product without a company restriction; failing that the system superuser
operands.constraints: the activity is assigned to the first of the three that exists

preconditions.condition: The routine runs as part of the scheduled replenishment work.
preconditions.otherwise: No reminder is raised, however many alert dates have passed.

procedure: Select every lot whose alert date is at or before today's date and whose reminded flag is false.
Restrict the selection to the lots that have at least one stock quantity record with a strictly positive quantity in a location whose usage is internal.
Schedule, for each remaining lot, a to-do activity with the summary "Alert Date Reached" and the note "The alert date has been reached for this lot/serial number".

Assign that activity to the product's responsible user as seen from the lot's company, or failing that to the product's responsible user without a company restriction, or failing that to the system superuser.

Set the reminded flag on every lot selected in the first step, including those the second step filtered out, so that a lot never produces two reminders even when its alert date is later moved backwards.

rounding.what: Nothing; the quantity test is a strict comparison with zero.
rounding.precision: The comparison with zero is made at the product's unit precision.

result.name: the activities scheduled and the lots marked as reminded
result.stored_or_displayed: stored as activities on the lots and as the reminded flag on every selected lot

edge_cases.case: A selected lot holds no stock in an internal location.
edge_cases.outcome: It receives no activity but is still marked as reminded, which is the asymmetry the routine deliberately keeps.

edge_cases.case: The alert date is later moved backwards on a lot already marked as reminded.
edge_cases.outcome: No second reminder is raised, because the selection skips lots whose flag is set.

edge_cases.case: The product has no responsible user for the lot's company.
edge_cases.outcome: The responsible user without a company restriction is used, and the system superuser when there is none.

edge_cases.case: The alert date is exactly today.
edge_cases.outcome: The lot is selected, because the comparison includes equality.

worked_examples.description: One run of the reminder over three lots
worked_examples.narrative: The first two lots are selected, the third being already reminded. Only the first holds stock in an internal location, so it alone receives an activity, yet both selected lots are marked as reminded.

records.name: The product count of a category
records.purpose: Counts the templates a category holds, its descendants included, which is the figure shown beside a category in the catalogue navigation.

operands.name: descendants of the category, itself included
operands.source: the category hierarchy
operands.constraints: the hierarchy holds no cycle, so the descendant set is finite

operands.name: number of templates whose category is exactly one descendant
operands.source: the grouping of templates by category, performed once over the whole descendant set of the categories being computed
operands.constraints: archived templates are excluded, because the grouping runs with the default active-record filter

preconditions.condition: The grouping covers every descendant of every category being computed.
preconditions.otherwise: A category would miss the templates of a descendant that was not in the grouping.

procedure: Group the templates by category once, over the whole descendant set of the categories being computed.
For each category, re-read its own descendants, itself included.
Add the grouped counts of those descendants.
Report the sum, which excludes archived templates because the grouping runs with the default active-record filter.
records.formula: product_count( category ) = sum over d in descendants( category ) including itself of number_of_templates_whose_category_is_exactly_d

rounding.what: Nothing; the result is a count of records.

result.name: product count of the category
result.stored_or_displayed: computed and displayed beside the category; not stored

edge_cases.case: A template is archived.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not counted, because the grouping runs with the default active-record filter.

edge_cases.case: A category has no template of its own but has descendants that do.
edge_cases.outcome: Its count is the sum over its descendants, which is greater than zero; the count includes descendants although the help text says otherwise, which is recorded as a compatibility finding in the domain document.

edge_cases.case: A category is a leaf with no template.
edge_cases.outcome: Its count is zero.

edge_cases.case: A template is moved to a descendant category.
edge_cases.outcome: The ancestor's count is unchanged, because the descendant is inside the sum.

worked_examples.description: A three-level hierarchy with archived and active templates
worked_examples.narrative: The leaf counts its own seven active templates and ignores the three archived ones. Its parent adds its own five, giving twelve, and the root adds its own two, giving fourteen.

records.name: The page count of a sheet of product labels
records.purpose: Works out how many pages a label print run needs, from the grid the chosen format declares and the number of copies asked for.

operands.name: columns and rows of the label grid
operands.source: the format string chosen for the print
operands.constraints: both strictly positive

operands.name: number of copies requested per product
operands.source: the print request
operands.constraints: summed over the products in the request

preconditions.condition: At least one label is requested.
preconditions.otherwise: The subtraction of one would make the arithmetic meaningless; a print of nothing produces no page.

preconditions.condition: The product is not a service.
preconditions.otherwise: Labels cannot be printed for it and the request is refused.

procedure: Multiply the number of columns by the number of rows to obtain the labels per page.
Add the copies requested for each product to obtain the total number of labels.
Subtract one from the total, divide by the labels per page discarding the remainder, and add one; that is the page count.
records.formula:
labels_per_page = columns × rows
total_labels    = sum over products of the number of copies requested for that product
page_count      = floor_div( total_labels − 1 , labels_per_page ) + 1

rounding.what: The division of the labels over the pages.
rounding.method: Division discarding the remainder, applied to the total less one, which is what makes an exactly full page count as one page rather than two.

result.name: page count
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed in the print preview and used to lay the printable document out

edge_cases.case: The total is exactly one page's worth.
edge_cases.outcome: The subtraction of one keeps the quotient at zero, so the count is one page.

edge_cases.case: The total is one more than a full page.
edge_cases.outcome: The quotient becomes one and the count is two pages.

edge_cases.case: One product is requested many times and another once.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the total matters; labels of different products share a page.

edge_cases.case: The product is a service.
edge_cases.outcome: The print is refused before any page count is computed.

worked_examples.description: A four-column, twelve-row format with sixty labels

inputs.format: four columns, twelve rows, price shown

worked_examples.narrative: Four multiplied by twelve is forty-eight labels a page. Sixty labels less one is fifty-nine, divided by forty-eight discarding the remainder is one, plus one is two pages.

worked_examples.description: The two boundary cases of the same format
worked_examples.narrative: Forty-eight less one is forty-seven, whose quotient by forty-eight is zero, so one page. Forty-nine less one is forty-eight, whose quotient is one, so two pages.

records.name: The preparation and ordering of a product's vendor lines
records.purpose: Assembles the vendor price lines a product may be bought on and puts them in the order the filtering walks, which fixes which line wins when several apply.

operands.name: vendor lines of the variant
operands.source: the variant's vendor price lines, read as a privileged reader
operands.constraints: kept when their company is empty or is the acting company, their partner is active, and they either name no variant or name this variant

operands.name: sequence of each line
operands.source: the vendor line
operands.constraints: sorted ascending, the first ordering key

operands.name: minimum quantity of each line
operands.source: the vendor line
operands.constraints: sorted descending, so that the most demanding tier is tried first

operands.name: price and identifier of each line
operands.unit_or_currency: the line's currency, and a whole number
operands.source: the vendor line
operands.constraints: price ascending then identifier ascending complete the ordering

preconditions.condition: The reader may read vendor price lines, or the read is performed as a privileged reader.
preconditions.otherwise: No line is visible and no vendor can be selected.

procedure: Read the variant's vendor lines as a privileged reader.
Keep the lines whose company is empty or is the acting company.
Keep the lines whose partner is active.
Keep the lines that either name no variant or name this variant.
Sort what remains by sequence ascending, then by minimum quantity descending, then by price ascending, then by identifier ascending.
records.formula:
prepared_lines = lines of the variant with ( company empty or company = acting_company ) and partner active and ( no variant named or the variant is this one )
ordering = sequence ascending , then minimum quantity descending , then price ascending , then identifier ascending

rounding.what: Nothing; the step selects and orders records.

result.name: the ordered list of candidate vendor lines
result.stored_or_displayed: consumed by the filtering; not stored

edge_cases.case: A line names another variant of the same template.
edge_cases.outcome: It is dropped at preparation, so it never competes for this variant.

edge_cases.case: A line's partner has been archived.
edge_cases.outcome: It is dropped, so an inactive vendor cannot be selected.

edge_cases.case: Two lines share a sequence and a minimum quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The lower price comes first, and the lower identifier breaks a remaining tie.

edge_cases.case: A line belongs to another company.
edge_cases.outcome: It is dropped, so vendor lines do not leak between companies.

worked_examples.description: Four lines ordered for one variant
worked_examples.narrative: The line whose partner is archived is dropped. Of the two lines of sequence ten, the one with the higher minimum quantity comes first, because minimum quantity is sorted descending; the line of sequence twenty comes last.

records.name: The filtering of vendor lines against a partner, a quantity, a date and a unit
records.purpose: Keeps the vendor lines that actually apply to a purchase of a stated quantity on a stated date, which is the set the selection then orders by price.

operands.name: quantity asked for
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit named by the caller, or the line's unit when none is named
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: converted into the line's unit when a unit was given and differs

operands.name: date
operands.source: the caller; today in the reader's time zone by default
operands.constraints: compared with each line's start and end dates

operands.name: partner
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: a line whose partner is neither that partner nor that partner's parent is skipped

operands.name: minimum quantity of the line
operands.source: the vendor line
operands.constraints: compared with the converted quantity at the `Product Unit` decimal precision

operands.name: forced unit demanded by the caller
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: a line whose unit is neither that unit nor the product's own unit is skipped

preconditions.condition: The lines have been prepared and ordered.
preconditions.otherwise: The walk would not be deterministic and the first kept line could differ between two systems.

procedure: Default the date to today in the reader's time zone and take the `Product Unit` decimal precision as the comparison precision.
Walk the prepared lines in order, converting the quantity into the line's unit when a unit was given and it differs from the line's unit.
Skip the line when its start date is after the date.
Skip the line when its end date is before the date.
Skip the line when the caller demanded a forced unit and the line's unit is neither that unit nor the product's own unit.
Skip the line when a partner was given and the line's partner is neither that partner nor that partner's parent.
Skip the line when the converted quantity is strictly less than the line's minimum quantity, compared at the `Product Unit` decimal precision.
Keep the line otherwise.
records.formula:
keep( line ) = ( line.start_date ≤ date or line has no start date )
  and ( line.end_date ≥ date or line has no end date )
  and ( no forced unit or line.unit ∈ { forced_unit , product_unit } )
  and ( no partner or line.partner ∈ { partner , partner.parent } )
  and ( converted_quantity ≥ line.minimum_quantity , compared at the Product Unit precision )
  and ( line names no variant or names this one )

rounding.what: The comparison of the converted quantity with the line's minimum quantity.
rounding.precision: The `Product Unit` decimal precision, two digits by default.
rounding.method: Comparison at that precision; no value is rewritten.
rounding.step: At the quantity test, after the unit conversion.

result.name: the kept vendor lines, in the prepared order
result.stored_or_displayed: consumed by the selection; not stored

edge_cases.case: The converted quantity equals the minimum quantity at the comparison precision.
edge_cases.outcome: The line is kept, because only a strictly smaller quantity is skipped.

edge_cases.case: The line has no start or end date.
edge_cases.outcome: The corresponding date test does not exclude it.

edge_cases.case: The partner given is a child contact of the line's partner.
edge_cases.outcome: The line is kept, because a line whose partner is the given partner's parent qualifies.

edge_cases.case: The caller names a unit the line does not use and the conversion is impossible.
edge_cases.outcome: No comparison can be made in that unit; the caller's forced-unit test skips the line first when a forced unit was demanded.
