expected_outputs.reason_line_43: its start date is after the date

worked_examples.narrative: One hundred and twenty is not strictly less than either minimum quantity, so both undated lines are kept; the third is skipped because it only starts the following year.

worked_examples.description: A purchase below the tier's minimum quantity

inputs.comparison_precision: the Product Unit precision, two digits

expected_outputs.reason: the quantity is strictly less than the minimum quantity

worked_examples.narrative: Fifty is strictly less than one hundred at the comparison precision, so the tier does not apply and the walk moves on to the next line.

records.name: The selection of the winning vendor line
records.purpose: Chooses one vendor line out of those that apply, keeping the walk to a single partner and then ordering that partner's lines by the price the buyer would actually pay.

operands.name: kept vendor lines, in the prepared order
operands.source: the filtering
operands.constraints: may be empty, in which case no vendor is selected

operands.name: partner of the first kept line
operands.source: the first kept line
operands.constraints: only lines of that same partner take part in the final ordering

operands.name: discounted price of each line converted into the acting company's currency
operands.source: the line's price after its discount, converted at the given date
operands.constraints: converted without rounding, which is what makes two close prices comparable

operands.name: field named by the caller for the ordering
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: when given, it is the first ordering key and the discounted price becomes the second

preconditions.condition: At least one line was kept.
preconditions.otherwise: No vendor is selected and the caller is told nothing applies.

procedure: Keep the first line of the filtered list and then every subsequent line belonging to the same partner as that first line.

Order that subset by the discounted price converted into the acting company's currency at the given date, without rounding, then by sequence, then by identifier, when the caller names no ordering field.
Order it by the field the caller names first, then by the discounted price, then by sequence, then by identifier, when the caller names one.
Return the first line of the ordered subset.
records.formula:
candidate_subset = { the first kept line } ∪ { subsequent kept lines whose partner = partner of the first kept line }
default_ordering = discounted price converted to the acting company's currency at the given date, without rounding , then sequence , then identifier
named_ordering   = the named field , then the discounted price , then sequence , then identifier
selected_line    = first of the ordered subset

rounding.what: The discounted price used for the ordering.
rounding.precision: None: the conversion into the acting company's currency is made without rounding.
rounding.method: No rounding, precisely so that two prices that would round to the same figure still order deterministically.
rounding.step: At the conversion, before the ordering.

result.name: the selected vendor line
result.stored_or_displayed: returned to the caller, which uses its partner, its price, its currency and its unit on the purchase document

edge_cases.case: The kept lines belong to several partners.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the partner of the first kept line competes; the prepared order therefore decides which vendor is considered at all.

edge_cases.case: Two lines of that partner have the same converted price.
edge_cases.outcome: The sequence and then the identifier break the tie.

edge_cases.case: The caller names an ordering field.
edge_cases.outcome: That field decides first and the price becomes the tie-breaker.

edge_cases.case: No line was kept.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is returned and the caller falls back to its own default, since the catalogue proposes no vendor.

worked_examples.description: Two tiers of one vendor and a line of another vendor
worked_examples.narrative: The cheaper line of the second vendor never competes, because the subset is restricted to the partner of the first kept line. Within that partner the lower converted price wins, giving seven point five zero.

records.name: The precisions and the rounding of every catalogue figure
records.purpose: Fixes, for each kind of figure the domain produces, which precision applies and how it is rounded, so that a rebuild rounds each figure in the same place and in the same way.

operands.name: sales price, cost, extra price, base price of a choice group and extra price of a combination item
operands.source: the templates, the variants, the Template Attribute Values, the choice groups and the combo items
operands.constraints: governed by the `Product Price` decimal precision, two digits by default

operands.name: prorated share of a choice group
operands.source: the proration of a combination product's price
operands.constraints: governed by the document currency's rounding multiple

operands.name: quantity compared in the vendor selection
operands.source: the purchase quantity and the vendor line's minimum quantity
operands.constraints: governed by the `Product Unit` decimal precision, two digits by default

operands.name: volume, weight and discount percentage
operands.unit_or_currency: a volume, a weight and a percentage
operands.source: the product fields
operands.constraints: governed by the `Volume`, `Stock Weight` and `Discount` decimal precisions, two digits by default

operands.name: measure read from a barcode
operands.source: the pattern match or the Global Standards One measure interpretation
operands.constraints: not governed by any precision

operands.name: expiry date arithmetic
operands.unit_or_currency: whole days added to or subtracted from a moment
operands.source: the product's day counts
operands.constraints: the time of day is preserved

preconditions.condition: The named decimal precisions are configured; their default digit counts are the ones the configuration document lists.
preconditions.otherwise: The default of two digits applies to each of them.

procedure: Round a sales price, a cost, an extra price, the base price of a choice group and the extra price of a combination item at the `Product Price` precision, half away from zero.
Round a prorated share at the document currency's rounding multiple, half away from zero, and give the remainder to the last choice group.
Compare a quantity in the vendor selection at the `Product Unit` precision, without rewriting either figure.
Round a volume at the `Volume` precision, a weight at the `Stock Weight` precision and a discount percentage at the `Discount` precision, each half away from zero.
Apply no rounding at all to a measure read from a barcode: the value is exactly the digits read with the decimal point inserted where the rule says.
Apply no rounding to expiry dates: whole days are added to or subtracted from a moment and the time of day is preserved.
records.formula:
money and prices → round to the `Product Price` precision, half away from zero
prorated share → round to the document currency's rounding multiple, half away from zero, remainder to the last choice group
quantities in the vendor selection → compare at the `Product Unit` precision
volume → `Volume` precision ; weight → `Stock Weight` precision ; discount → `Discount` precision, each half away from zero
barcode-derived measure → no rounding
expiry dates → whole days, time of day preserved

rounding.what: Every figure the domain produces, by kind.
rounding.precision: `Product Price`, `Product Unit`, `Volume`, `Stock Weight` and `Discount`, two digits each by default; the document currency's rounding multiple for a prorated share.
rounding.method: Half away from zero everywhere a figure is rounded; comparison only for quantities; none for barcode measures and expiry dates.
rounding.step: At display and at storage for prices; at each share for the proration, with the remainder corrected afterwards; at the comparison for quantities; never for barcode measures and dates.

result.name: the rounded figure of each kind
result.unit_or_currency: the currency, unit or measure of the figure concerned
result.stored_or_displayed: stored or displayed as the field that carries it

edge_cases.case: A price carries more digits than the precision after a division.
edge_cases.outcome: It is rounded half away from zero when it is stored or displayed; the intermediate arithmetic keeps its digits.

edge_cases.case: A prorated share leaves a residue.
edge_cases.outcome: The residue goes to the last choice group in sequence order, so the shares add up exactly.

edge_cases.case: A weight read from a barcode has three decimals while the weight precision has two.
edge_cases.outcome: The barcode value is not rounded here; any rounding is the consuming domain's, applied when the quantity is stored.

edge_cases.case: A quantity is compared with a tier's minimum quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison is made at the `Product Unit` precision and neither figure is rewritten.

worked_examples.description: One figure of each kind, rounded by its own rule

inputs.barcode_measure_digits: 002004 with a decimal position of two

expected_outputs.quantity_comparison_at_two_digits: 120.00 is not less than 120.00, so the tier applies

worked_examples.narrative: The price and the share are rounded half away from zero at two digits; the quantity is only compared, at the same two digits, so the four thousandths do not decide the tier; the barcode measure keeps exactly the digits scanned; and the expiry arithmetic keeps the time of day.

records.name: The moments and the rounding of the currency conversions of this domain
records.purpose: Says which date each currency conversion of the catalogue uses and which of them is made without rounding, since the same amount converted at two different moments gives two different figures.

operands.name: base price of a choice group
operands.source: the minimum over the group's items
operands.constraints: converted at the current moment

operands.name: supplement shown on a matrix header cell
operands.source: the values the header cell stands for
operands.constraints: converted at today's date, which is the current moment for this purpose

operands.name: converted base price and item supplement of a combination product's proration
operands.unit_or_currency: the choice group's currency and the item's currency
operands.source: the proration
operands.constraints: converted at the document date

operands.name: discounted price used to order the vendor lines
operands.source: the vendor selection
operands.constraints: converted at the given date and without rounding

preconditions.condition: A rate is available for the pair of currencies at the moment or date used.
preconditions.otherwise: The multi-currency domain decides which rate applies; the catalogue does not choose one of its own.

procedure: Convert the base price of a choice group at the current moment, which makes it a live figure that is deliberately not stored.
Convert the supplement of a matrix header cell at today's date.
Convert the base prices and the item supplements of a proration at the document date, which makes a prorated document stable when it is re-read.
Convert the discounted price used to order the vendor lines at the given date and without rounding.
Delegate every one of these conversions to the multi-currency domain rather than computing a rate here.
records.formula:
combo base price and matrix header cell → convert at the current moment
combo proration and vendor ordering → convert at the document date or the given date
vendor ordering → convert without rounding
every other conversion → round to the target currency's rounding multiple, half away from zero

rounding.what: The converted amounts.
rounding.precision: The target currency's rounding multiple, except for the vendor ordering, which is not rounded at all.
rounding.method: Half away from zero where rounding applies.
rounding.step: At each conversion; the vendor ordering deliberately keeps the unrounded figure so that two close prices order deterministically.

result.name: the converted amount of each conversion
result.stored_or_displayed: displayed on the choice group, the matrix cell and the document lines; only the prorated shares are stored

edge_cases.case: A rate changes between two reads of a choice group.
edge_cases.outcome: Its base price changes, because the conversion is made at the current moment; this is why the figure is not stored.

edge_cases.case: A document is re-read after a rate change.
edge_cases.outcome: Its prorated shares are unchanged, because the conversion used the document date.

edge_cases.case: Two vendor lines convert to amounts that would round to the same figure.
edge_cases.outcome: The unrounded conversion still orders them, and the sequence and identifier break a true tie.

edge_cases.case: The target currency equals the source currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion is an identity and no rounding is introduced.

worked_examples.description: The same supplement converted for a matrix cell and for a document line

inputs.target_currency: a currency worth 1.2345 units per euro today and 1.2000 units per euro at the document date

worked_examples.narrative: The matrix cell converts at today's rate, giving six point one seven two five rounded to six point one seven. The document line converts at the document date's rate, giving exactly six. The two figures differ legitimately, because the two conversions use different moments.

worked_examples.description: Two vendor lines ordered on their unrounded converted prices
worked_examples.narrative: Both prices would round to seven point five zero, so rounding before the ordering would make the choice depend on the tie-breakers alone; the conversion is made without rounding precisely so that the cheaper line wins.
